articles.title: LeBron's Fanatics Deal Includes Helicopter Use
articles.summary: The helicopter has repeatedly gone between NYC and Philly.
articles.body:
LeBron James isn't paying a dime for his commute to and from Philadelphia to play for the Sixers.

A Fanatics source told Front Office Sports that James has been using the company's aviation as part of his broader deal with the company. James signed a multiyear trading card partnership with Fanatics in January 2024, while he agreed to a deal with the Sixers in July and will reportedly live in New York City while playing for the team.

He has been seen taking a helicopter with multiple Fanatics logos to and from Philadelphia.

"The deal we signed with Fanatics almost three years ago includes access to their corporate aviation," a spokesperson for James told FOS . "It's a feature in many of their deals with their largest athletes and we appreciate their partnership as LeBron splits his time between New York and Philadelphia."

A one-way chopper from New York City to Philadelphia is about $4,000 to $10,000 . It's not known how much Fanatics's deal with James is worth.

Flight records show the Fanatics helicopter James has used made a dozen round-trips between Philadelphia and New York in the past week. A one-way trip normally takes about 30 minutes, cutting what is normally about a 90-minute to two-hour drive.

James, who has made nearly $600 million in his 24-year NBA career, signed a two-year, $8 million deal with the Sixers in July. He will earn a career-low $3.87 million this season.

But he's making it back through several endorsement deals, including with Fanatics and a recent deal with Polymarket that FOS reported last month is worth about $15 million annually.

articles.title: Fantasy Football Waiver Wire, Week 5: Will Shipley, Dohnte Meyers among top pickups
articles.summary: Justin Boone takes you through his top fantasy football waiver wire options for Week 5.
articles.body:
Every Monday during the season, Justin Boone breaks down the recommended waiver-wire pickups.

Roster percentages are generated from Yahoo leagues. Free-Agent Budget (FAB) amounts are based on a $100 salary cap. Only players rostered in less than 50% of leagues are considered.

Brissett hasn't picked up where he left off last season, when he was a top-10 fantasy quarterback on a per game basis over the final 12 games. Fortunately, a matchup with the banged-up Lions secondary is the perfect recipe for any passer.

Through four weeks, Detroit has allowed at least 20 fantasy points to every quarterback the unit has faced, including Tyler Shough (QB6 in Week 1), Josh Allen (QB1 in Week 2), Geno Smith (QB3 in Week 3) and Bryce Young (QB6 in Week 4 with only Monday Night Football remaining).

Brissett is an excellent streaming option this week, just be careful about expecting any long-term solutions from him. Arizona will take on the Broncos, Rams (twice), Seahawks and Chiefs in five of the next six outings. If Brissett struggles and continues to turn the ball over (three interceptions this week), the Cardinals will likely see what they have in rookie Carson Beck down the stretch.

C.J. Stroud i s 58% rostered but would be the No. 1 QB add if available.

Sam Darnold i s 53% rostered but would be the No. 2 QB add behind Stroud, if available.

Desperation streaming options (if starter is out)

The trainer's room is a busy place in Philadelphia, with DeVonta Smith and Dallas Goedert ruled out for Week 4, and Saquon Barkley joining them on the sidelines during the game due to a hamstring injury.

Bigsby handled the majority of the work from that point on, totaling 55 yards on 14 carries in the loss with Shipley being the preferred passing-down back. To complicate the situation even more, Bigsby left the game late in the fourth quarter with an injury of his own and now is reportedly headed for an IR stint .

The initial updates on Barkley suggest it's not a serious injury, but any hamstring ailment can result in a missed game or two. For the time being, Shipley needs to be a priority add in case Barkley can't suit up next week, even though the Jaguars' run defense isn't an ideal opponent for a spot start on Sunday.

If Barkley is out, Shipley will be a fantasy RB3 with low-end RB2 upside given the banged up state of the offense. In that scenario, the Eagles would likely elevate either Dameon Pierce or Jaydon Blue from their practice squad to back him up.

With Jadarian Price being placed on injured reserve, Wilson became a priority add in the lead up to Week 4. He answered the call with 21 carries for 81 rushing yards and a touchdown, as well as another 39 yards and a receiving TD on three receptions.

That's a better spot start than any fantasy manager could have hoped for, but the Seahawks' backfield is constantly evolving week to week. The latest change came in the form of reportedly signing Mixon .

It was long believed Mixon's career was over due to a foot injury, but the 30-year-old is attempting a comeback. He's worth stashing now to see if he's healthy enough to take on a big role in this backfield. Just remember, there's a plenty of former stars who have struggled when returning from a long layoff near the end of their careers.

We also have to factor in Zach Charbonnet, who had his practice window opened last week. However, head coach Mike Macdonald has already suggested that Charbonnet won't play in Week 5.

This all boils down to at least one more start for Wilson before Charbonnet and possibly Mixon get involved. Sadly, the end result here is heading towards some sort of committee in the second half of the season, which will limit the ceilings of every Seattle back.

Despite saving his fantasy day yet again with a touchdown, Omarion Hampton's usage continues to trend in the wrong direction. This week, the three-man committee played nearly even snaps with Mitchell (26), Hampton (25) and Kimani Vidal (25) sharing the backfield.

Hampton still led the way in fantasy production by turning his 11 touches into 53 scrimmage yards and a score, but Mitchell saw the most volume overall with 15 touches and 63 yards. Even Vidal had a solid outing with 36 yards and a receiving TD on seven chances.

This type of deployment makes it difficult to project usage and stat lines for the Chargers backs on a weekly basis. However, it's clear Mitchell is a favorite of offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel, who reportedly pounded the table to add him in the offseason. Given Mitchell's uptick in volume and gamebreaking speed, he should be picked up as an upside RB3/flex to see how this develops in the coming weeks.

Woody Marks is 55% rostered but would be the No. 3 RB add behind Wilson and Bigsby, if available.

Best one-injury away backup RBs to stash

Chris Rodriguez Jr. vs. PHI (37% rostered)

Washington has become a regular part of the waiver wire column, since he still remains available in almost 70% of leagues. That's despite averaging 55 receiving yards per game through the opening month.

Now, the 25-year-old is coming off his best outing of the season with five catches and 67 yards against the Vikings. He's also earned target shares of 28% and 29% over the last two weeks, which is especially important in Miami's low-volume passing attack.

This isn't a league-winning waiver wire pickup, but Washington can be a solid WR3/flex in your lineup as bye weeks begin.

This isn't the first time we've seen DJ Moore leave a game due to injury, only to have Coleman step up. The first time that occurred was in Week 2, when Coleman posted 63 yards and six receptions. On Sunday, the results were even better with Coleman catching six of his seven targets for 116 yards and a touchdown.

It's a one-game sample, but this was the best version of Coleman I can remember watching as a Bills fan. He looked more crisp on his routes and was getting some snaps out of the slot.

Coleman's path to being a star disappeared a long time ago, but he's now shown us on two separate occasions that he can fill in when injuries require it. While there weren't many silver linings to take away from this loss for Buffalo, Coleman's performance was a positive step towards him being a more capable second or third option in the offense.

For fantasy, you're picking him up in case Moore's aggravation leads to missed time. I'll update this article when we get an update on his status.

Even before Ladd McConkey aggravated his foot injury, Harris had taken on a bigger role in the Chargers offense this year. The 24-year-old wideout has topped 50 yards in each of his last three games while playing 77% of the snaps on the year. That includes a season-high 93% snap share in Week 4 when McConkey left early.

Harris now has 13 catches for 209 yards on 21 targets through four games. He's outproduced Quentin Johnston, who has just seven catches for 108 yards.

Investing in the Chargers' passing attack might not seem that exciting given Justin Herbert's struggles so far, but Harris is a low-risk pickup capable of returning fantasy WR3 value if McConkey sits out.

The Bengals lost both their star wideouts to injuries on Sunday. Ja'Marr Chase's status is up in the air as he'll try to clear concussion protocol this week. Meanwhile, Tee Higgins is dealing with an adductor injury that's put him on the doubtful side to suit up in Week 5.

That allowed Meyers to see nine targets against the Jaguars, hauling in seven of them for 82 yards.

If I told you Joe Burrow's potential No. 1 receiver might be available on the waiver wire right before a favorable matchup with the Dolphins, is that something you might be interested in?

The market for Hill is reportedly heating up , with many people connecting the dots to his former team the Chiefs. Kansas City just lost Rashee Rice (short-term) and Tyquan Thornton (long-term) to injury, which creates a clear need at the position.

However, let's make one thing clear: this is not prime Tyreek Hill. Even prior to suffering a torn ACL, left knee dislocation and multiple other torn ligaments, the 32-year-old was a declining player.

Even so, if he's healthy and lands on a contender like the Chiefs, he could return fantasy WR3 value with some potential upside. This is still a stash and see situation, so don't let your expectations run wild until we find out where he signs and whether he's anywhere close to his past form.

With Ja'Marr Chase in concussion protocol and Tee Higgins unlikely to play in Week 5 due to his adductor injury, Gesicki is back in play as a fantasy starter.

In their absence, Gesicki found the end zone for the third time this season. He now has three solid stat lines in four games, with 5-78-1, 3-37-1 and 3-40-1.

This week also marks a revenge game for Gesicki against the Dolphins. In his last meeting with Miami, he scored a touchdown as well. If both Chase and Higgins are sidelined, Gesicki will be a fantasy TE1 this week. If Chase manages to play, Gesicki will still be a strong high-end TE2 streamer.

Herbert has yet to reach 14 fantasy points in a single game this season. He's also been held to 226 passing yards or less and hasn't accounted for more than one touchdown in any outing. There are far better options at quarterback.

When he returns, this backfield will look completely different with Zach Charbonnet eventually returning and the team flirting with free agents. At best, Price will be locked in a committee in the second half of the season, which limits his potential in Year 1.

articles.title: Is Ben Johnson Bears' Most Important Piece? Why Last 2 Games Suggest He Might Be
articles.summary: Colin Cowherd said he believes that Sunday's performance is the latest piece of evidence of who matters most in Chicago: Head coach Ben Johnson.
articles.body: The Chicago Bears are 3-1 and have won three games this season with three different starting quarterbacks. With that, Colin Cowherd believes Sunday's performance is the latest piece of evidence of who matters most in Chicago: Head coach Ben Johnson. "It is a quarterback-first league, but the guy who builds the culture is the coach," Cowherd said on Monday's "The Herd." "I think we've discovered in the last two weeks, as gifted as Caleb Williams is, the centerpiece of the Bears is Ben Johnson." With quarterback Caleb Williams sidelined for a second straight game with a right hamstring injury, the Bears won against the New York Jets 23-12. Backup quarterback Tyson Bagent, who threw for 268 yards, and second-year running back Kyle Monangai, who carried a career-high 30 times for 146 yards and two touchdowns, led the way in the victory. "Yesterday, a backup running back, a seventh-round running back, with a backup quarterback. Once again, it's 400-plus yards. I mean, they had more first downs than the Jets had plays," Cowherd said. "So don't look at the 23-12 score. This could have been 50-12. It was not competitive." New York finished with just 157 yards and seven first downs and went 0-for-7 on third down. Cowherd pointed to the time of possession, with the Bears holding the ball for nearly 43 minutes, calling it, "like a lopsided college time of possession differential." The Bears finished with 492 yards of offense and 232 rushing yards against the Jets. They set a franchise record with 34 first downs and did not record a punt in a game for the first time since 2014. Cowherd also pointed to the Bears' commitment to the run under Johnson. "It is the fifth time since Ben Johnson, the Ben Johnson era, the fifth time they have had over 220 rushing yards. This is not the 80s. This is not the 90s. That is a ton of rushing yards today." Chicago won on Monday night in Week 3, 27-7 over the Eagles, with 38-year-old Case Keenum at quarterback. Keenum threw for 247 yards and two touchdowns in that game. Cowherd credited Johnson's system, rather than any single player, for the Bears' 3-1 start. "[Johnson]'s done it with an old quarterback who we thought was retired, Case Keenum, who was 11-for-11 against the blitz. He's done it with a backup in Bagent. He's done it with Caleb Williams stylistically. It just doesn't matter," Cowherd said. "I'm in no way marginalizing Caleb Williams." Cowherd went on to compare Johnson to other offensive minds he believes define their franchises across the league. "The centerpiece of this franchise, and I've said it with the Rams — got to a Super Bowl with [Jared] Goff, got to a Super Bowl with [Matthew] Stafford. The centerpiece is McVay," Cowherd said. "Kyle Shanahan got [Jimmy] Garoppolo to a Super Bowl. Kyle Shanahan is the centerpiece of the 49ers. "I think Liam Coen does a great job. He has shown that leaving Tampa, their circle in the drain, goes to Jacksonville and elevates Trevor Lawrence. There are these offensive coaches that I think are just separating themselves from all other coaches in the league." articles.title: White Sox Win Again: 3 Takeaways With The Guardians Now On The Brink
articles.summary: The Guardians have their backs to the wall with the White Sox now just one win away from the ALCS.
articles.body: Two years ago, the White Sox set a modern-day record with 121 losses. Last year, they suffered through a third straight 100-loss season. Now, they’re one win away from advancing to the American League Championship Series for the first time since winning the World Series in 2005. Here are my takeaways from Chicago’s 4-3 Game 2 ALDS win over the Guardians: 1. Williams' Outing Spoiled By Bullpen After dropping the first game of the series with their Rookie of the Year and Cy Young contender on the mound, the Guardians took solace in knowing that Gavin Williams would follow Parker Messick in Game 2. Williams, who led the American League in strikeouts this year, did his job. The burly right-hander struck out 11, tied for the second-most ever for a Guardians pitcher in a playoff game behind only Charles Nagy’s 12 strikeouts in the 1996 ALDS, and then watched his lead immediately disappear from the dugout on Monday night. After a leadoff single by White Sox third baseman Miguel Vargas to start the sixth inning, Williams — who threw 99 pitches or more 10 times this season — was pulled at 98 pitches. "We couldn't have asked anything more from Gavin tonight," said Guardians manager Stephen Vogt. "He did his job and then some." After his departure, Chicago’s hitters seemed to breathe a sigh of relief. A Cleveland bullpen that ranked third in the American League in ERA and first in MLB in strikeout rate this season was unable to build a bridge to star closer Cade Smith. Erik Sabrowski, who allowed an RBI double to Colson Montgomery in Cleveland’s Game 1 loss, entered the game and got a groundout before walking a batter, throwing a wild pitch, getting a flyout and then surrendering a go-ahead, two-run, two-out double to rookie Braden Montgomery. Vogt then turned to reliever Hunter Gaddis, who promptly surrendered an RBI single to Chase Meidroth for an extra — and, ultimately, vital — White Sox insurance run. Cleveland seemed to hold the obvious bullpen advantage entering the series, but it hasn’t played out that way. 2. Relievers Shut Down 'Guards Ball' The ball chopped in front of home plate and hovered in the air for what had to feel like hours to White Sox pitcher Sean Newcomb, who corralled the first-inning grounder from Nathaniel Lowe behind the pitcher’s mound, turned, then pulled his throw so far down the line that first baseman Munetaka Murakami couldn’t even muster an effort to stretch for it. This was "Guards Ball" in action, an encapsulation of a Cleveland team that has won three straight division titles despite an offense that routinely ranks among the league’s least powerful. But it’s a dangerous way to live in October, and a Cleveland offense that has mustered just three runs and seven hits through two games could again be its undoing. Game 2 began with White Sox starter Anthony Kay allowing two of the first three Guardians batters to reach, first on a seeing-eye single from Steven Kwan and then on a free pass. Newcomb entered and failed to extinguish the threat. He got behind on Jo Adell, eventually intentionally walking the Guardians outfielder to load the bases, before inducing the grounder he was seeking from Lowe. But his errant throw sailed into right field and allowed two runs to score and gave life to a meager Cleveland offense that was held scoreless in Game 1 and a Guardians home crowd that, to that point in the series, had little reason to get involved. Sean Burke, the bulk pitcher in yet another White Sox bullpen game, would restore order. Burke allowed just one run over 5.1 innings, at one point retiring 13 straight, buying time for the White Sox offense to dig its way out of an early hole. Then Grant Taylor, two days after throwing 42 pitches in a career-high four shutout innings to finish off the Guardians in Game 1, returned for more. Taylor allowed an RBI triple to Jo Adell in the eighth inning then shut the door on the Guardians, recording the final four outs to send the series back to Chicago with his team up 2-0. 3. Young Sluggers Rising To Occasion In Game 1 of the ALDS, Murakami had the two hardest-hit balls of the day. The first was a single. The second was a two-run, 440-foot tank to start the scoring off Messick, who had allowed just three home runs over the final eight starts of his sensational season. In Game 2, Murakami picked up where he left off, starting the scoring again for the White Sox. This time, he turned on a 99.5-mph fastball from Williams, lacing it 106.4 mph off the bat to right field for an RBI single that cut the deficit in half. Murakami has now knocked in at least one run in three of his first four playoff games, an auspicious sign for a White Sox team that needs him to be a difference maker. But the 26-year-old former NPB standout is far from the only young White Sox hitter contributing to Chicago’s stellar start to the postseason. Meidroth, 25, is hitting .400 with five RBI through four playoff games. Colson Montgomery, 24, has homered and doubled. Rookie Braden Montgomery, 23, delivered the big knock on Monday, and 26-year-old All-Star Miguel Vargas has already reached base six times in the ALDS. 3 1/2. What's Next? This is obviously a nightmare scenario for the Guardians, not only because they dropped both games at home but also because they couldn’t secure a win with either of their two best starters. Now, they’ll have to turn to Tanner Bibee, deadline addition Foster Griffin — who had a 3.06 ERA with the Nationals and a 5.19 ERA in nine starts with the Guardians — or a combination of bullpen arms to save their season. If they can’t find a way to generate some offense, though, it won’t matter who’s throwing. "Backs against the wall, this is where this team thrives," Vogt said. "You don't want to be in this position. I’m not going to sugarcoat it. We've backed ourselves into a corner. We know that. If there's anything I know about this group of guys, it’s that we love challenges like this. We are going to embrace it."

articles.title: EXCLUSIVE | 'Fear may never completely go away': Sujeet Kalkal on turning Olympic heartbreak into Asian Games gold
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Two years ago, Sujeet Kalkal was stranded at Dubai International Airport, watching his Olympic dream slip away with every passing hour.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Two years ago, Sujeet Kalkal was stranded at Dubai International Airport, watching his Olympic dream slip away with every passing hour.On his way to Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, for the Asian Olympic Qualifying Tournament, Kalkal was stuck in Dubai for three days after floods disrupted his travel plans. By the time a flight was arranged, it was too late. He could not reach Bishkek in time, and with it went his chance to qualify for the Paris Olympics.Two years later, the disappointment of Dubai has been replaced by an Asian Games gold. Kalkal, the world No. 2 in the men's 65kg category, fought back from 2-9 down against Tajikistan's Abdulmazhid Kudiev in the final to win 10-9, ending India's eight-year wait for a wrestling gold at the Games.The comeback was symbolic of what Kalkal's career has looked like since that Olympic setback. He has had to rebuild, compete through the disappointment and find a way back to the biggest stages. On Sunday, he did that with an Asian Games title.When the final whistle came, Kalkal folded his hands, looked up and thanked God. He then took a lap of the arena with the Indian tricolour draped around his shoulders, tears and a broad smile.For a wrestler who had once been denied even the chance to fight for an Olympic place, the moment carried a little more weight than an Asian Games gold."This gold means a lot to me. Not just because it is an Asian Games gold, but because there is so much behind this medal. The last few years have had many ups and downs, and I missed a few opportunities, but I never lost belief in myself," Kalkal told TimesofIndia.com in an exclusive interview on his way back to Imlota village in Bhiwani, Haryana, where his parents were waiting to welcome him.The Dubai episode, he says, is now behind him. What remains is the lesson from it - and a much bigger target."Paris was very difficult for me to miss, but that experience made me stronger instead of breaking me. LA 2028 is obviously a very big goal for me," Kalkal said.And he is clear about what he wants from that opportunity. "Olympics mein jaana hai toh sirf participate karne ke liye nahi jaana, bhaisaab. Gold ke liye jaana hai [“If you’re going to the Olympics, don’t go just to participate, brother. Go there to win gold]."India had not won a wrestling gold at the Asian Games since 2018. Kalkal's victory ended that wait and added another major title to a career that already includes an U23 World Championship crown, Asian Championships success and a Zagreb Open triumph."India has won a wrestling gold at the Asian Games after eight years, so being a part of it is very special for me. This medal reminds me that if you keep working hard, your time will come," he said.The road to the Asian Games gold was not easy for Kalkal. He had a challenging draw, but handled each bout with confidence.After a comfortable opening victory, he made a statement in the quarterfinals by throwing Iran's Abbas Ebrahimzadehsavadkouhi from a standing position within the opening 20 seconds.The semifinal brought an even bigger test, but Kalkal overcame Olympic champion Kotaro Kiyooka to reach the gold medal bout.Then came the final against Tajikistan's Abdulmazhid Kudiev, and it looked like the toughest challenge of them all.Instead of allowing the deficit to affect him, Kalkal fought his way back into the contest. He produced eight points to turn a seven-point deficit into a 10-9 victory and seal the Asian Games title."The simple plan was to wrestle my own way and not be impressed by my opponent's name. Whether he is an Olympic champion, a world champion or anyone else, everyone starts from zero on the mat. I just trusted my preparation and my strength. I knew that if I executed my best, I could beat anyone. Instead of thinking too much during the match, I just had to fight for every single point," he said.Kalkal also dedicated the gold to the country and remembered his father, who stood by him throughout his journey."I dedicate this gold to the whole of India. Of course, my first call was to my father. He has supported me tremendously throughout this journey, and without his support, it would have been impossible for me to reach this point. His support will always remain with me," the Indian wrestler said.The final also reflected the mental change Kalkal says came from the disappointment of 2024."Fear may never completely go away, but now I know how to fight with fear. When you go through tough situations in life, small things stop bothering you. What happened in Dubai, missing the Olympic qualifiers - every experience taught me something," the Indian wrestler said."Now I don't run away from pressure. I enjoy pressure because those are the moments when you realise how strong you actually are," Kalkal said.The Asian Games gold now joins an already impressive list of achievements for Kalkal, but he is not dwelling on the medals he has already won. The next target is Los Angeles. And this time, he wants to get there on his own terms."Gold ke liye jaana hai."Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Other side of India's Asian Games success: 201 athletes won just 6 bronze, 137 returned empty-handed
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India’s 85-medal haul at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games was its secondbest finish, but the headline numbers don’t reveal everything.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India’s 85-medal haul at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games was its secondbest finish, but the headline numbers don’t reveal everything.A sport-by-sport audit by TOI shows that 137 Indian athletes across 16 disciplines returned empty-handed, exposing persistent gaps in the country’s medal ambitions.India’s pruned-down 495-member contingent competed across 36 sport disciplines and finished fourth with 21 gold, 27 silver and 37 bronze medals.Yet 137 athletes across 16 disciplines won nothing.Another 64 athletes across six sports managed six bronze — one each in kurash, mixed martial arts, rowing, sepaktakraw, soft tennis and wushu. The zero-medal list included canoeing (19 athletes), cycling (14), equestrian (7), esports (15), fencing (20), gymnastics (1), judo (3), karate (2), rugby sevens (13), sport climbing (2), surfing (4), swimming (12), taekwondo (3), tennis (7), teqball (3) and volleyball (12). The six-bronze group comprised kurash (6 athletes), MMA (2), rowing (22), sepaktakraw (21), soft tennis (6) and wushu (7).In all, 201 athletes accounted for just six bronze medals across the 22 disciplines mentioned above. In other prominent sports with sizable athlete numbers, table tennis sent 10 athletes and returned with one bronze and badminton’s 20-member contingent managed one bronze in the men’s team event. Together, the two sent 37 athletes and produced only two bronze.India contested in 259 medal events in AichiNagoya and won medals in just 20, a 7.7% eventpodium conversion rate. Of 356 medals available in which India featured, the nation collected 85, a conversion rate of only 23.9%.The spending breakdownThe govt spent Rs 259.69 crore on 19 sports as part of the overall total expenditure during the current Asian Games cycle (Nov 2023-Aug 2026), led by badminton (Rs 49.26 cr), cycling track (Rs 35.9 cr), fencing (Rs 28.2 cr), table tennis (Rs 25.3 cr), tennis (Rs 22.4 cr) and canoe/kayak (Rs 20.1 cr). Other allocations included rowing (Rs 13.8 cr,) swimming (Rs 10.8 cr), gymnastics (Rs 10.49 cr), judo (Rs 8.05 cr), wushu (Rs 7.8 cr), volleyball (Rs 6.5 cr), sepaktakraw (Rs 5.7 cr), equestrian (Rs 3.7 cr), rugby (Rs 3.63 cr), surfing (Rs 2.9 cr), karate (Rs 1.99 cr), soft tennis (Rs 1.6 cr) and kurash (Rs 1.6 cr).On three sports – MMA, eSports and sport climbing, the govt spent no money. As per the govt’s own estimates, it spent approximately Rs 703 cr across 30 disciplines during the Nov 2023-Aug 2026 preparation cycle. The Rs 703 cr included about Rs 118 cr for domestic training and national coaching camps, Rs 40 cr for overseas training, Rs 252 cr for international competition exposure, Rs 89 cr for equipment, Rs 86 cr for foreign coaches/support staff and Rs 118 cr for other expenses, including Indian experts, championships, competitions in India, grassroots and coach development.Also, a total of 427 athletes who were part of the govt’s various programmes and schemes participated in the Games, including 77 athletes from Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS) Core group, 78 from TOPS Development 78, 48 from Target Asian Games Group (TAGG), 65 Khelo India Athlete (KIA), 25 from National Centre of Excellence (NCoE) and 134 from National Coaching Camps (NCCs).The Glasgow comparison is revealing, though not like-for-like. India had 122 athletes and para-athletes in 10 sports at the curtailed 2026 Commonwealth Games and won 39 medals — 13 gold, 17 silver and nine bronze — also finishing fourth. The Asian Games contingent was 4.06 times larger, but its 85-medal haul was only 2.18 times Glasgow’s. Medal efficiency was 17.2 per 100 athletes in Aichi-Nagoya against 32 in Glasgow.The message is that at this level, the medal base remains concentrated.For a country investing Rs 703 cr across a multi-year cycle, the next challenge is clear: turn wider participation, exposure and support into wider podium conversion.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: In Japan, women’s sumo battles tradition and a male-dominated system for survival
articles.summary: KYOTO: It’s a rainy Sunday morning but that hasn’t stopped more than 100 women and girls from making their way to the Kyoto City Budo Centre, Japan’s
articles.body: KYOTO: It’s a rainy Sunday morning but that hasn’t stopped more than 100 women and girls from making their way to the Kyoto City Budo Centre, Japan’s oldest martial arts performance hall. Built in 1899, the original structure is mostly out of bounds for visitors. But a recently built adjoining hall is buzzing with activity.The women are dressed in wrestling singlets, wearing the traditional mawashi, the thick belt associated with sumo, over it. At the centre of the hall is a ring that looks like a dohyo, the raised platform on which sumo is contested. It looks like one. But it isn’t.Women are traditionally barred from stepping into a sumo dohyo, a practice rooted in religious beliefs that have long associated menstruation with impurity. Yet, inside this hall, women are doing precisely what tradition has told them they cannot: sumo wrestling.More than 600 women in over 70 clubs practise the traditional form of wrestling in Japan, despite the resistance it has faced. In the wrestling venue at the Asian Games, when a senior official of the Japan Wrestling Association was asked about women’s sumo, he laughed before dismissing it: “It’s no sport for women.”But it wasn’t always this way. Historical research suggests women participated in sumo as far back as the fifth century. The sport also had periods of popularity between 1603 and 1868 and in the early 20th century, before women’s sumo was banned in 1926 on moral and traditional grounds.It returned in organised form in 1997. Yet, amateur women’s sumo continues to fight for survival. The Japan Sumo Association does not recognise it, leaving private clubs, schools and universities to keep it alive.At universities and a few clubs, women train alongside their male counterparts. Even the arrival of Japan’s first female prime minister has not changed the equation. Sanae Takaichi, who became prime minister last year, had said, “I respect tradition. I will not step on the dohyo.”There are, however, women like Airi Hisano, considered the strongest woman sumo wrestler of the country, trying to change things. The 27-yearold Tokyo native began with karate and judo before finding her calling in sumo at Nihon University.She was fortunate to find support at home. “My family wants me to do my best,” she said.It wasn’t easy. “Of course people made fun of me because, in rigid gender spaces, acceptance wasn’t easy. But that didn’t bother me. Also, it wasn’t an Olympic sport,” said Airi, who works in the administrative section of Tachihi Holdings.A heavyweight competitor, Airi balances training with her day job, where she also doubles as a security guard. She holds a third-degree black belt in judo and a first-degree black belt in karate. “We still have a long way to go,” she said.Not far from where Airi was preparing for her bout, Katsumasa Kawase was putting three girls from Team Shiga through their warm-up. “Being a sumo wrestler myself, I didn’t want my daughters to be denied the opportunity when they wanted to try it,” Kawase said, helping his daughters Momoka and Yuzuki warm up.The physical demands are no different from those faced by their male counterparts. The typical diet includes chicken or pork, vegetables, rice and candied sweet potatoes. But muscle is not the biggest hurdle. Awareness is.Morita, who handles public relations for Yoko Sumo Club, an all-women’s team based in Tokyo, said the club was formed in 2024 and has remained exclusively female. “A major challenge is that many people are still unfamiliar with women’s sumo,” she said.What keeps the wrestlers going? “They continue believing that the sport will eventually be included in the Olympics,” Morita said.Women coaches are still few. One of them is Mao Ueda of Hirakata Sumo Club. A former judoka and jiu-jitsu practitioner, she took up coaching after seeing an opportunity to combine her experience in martial arts with the nuances of sumo.“It’s a long road,” she said. The biggest challenge, she believes, comes after university. “With no recognition, money or future, most girls drop out after university. We need a structure to change that,” Ueda said.However, Momoka, 9, knows little about any of that. articles.summary: WWE RAW aired its October 5 episode from the Enterprise Center in St. Louis, Missouri.
articles.body: WWE RAW aired its October 5 episode from the Enterprise Center in St. Louis, Missouri. This was the go-home show for their upcoming Premium Live Event, Money in the Bank 2026. Roman Reigns returned to handle family business while continuing his feud with LA Knight heading into the WWE PLE. He also brought back Solo Sikoa to team up with The Usos for a match against 946.Plus, other exciting matches took place, and a chaotic main event concluded with a new match made official for Money in the Bank.What happened in the opening segment of WWE RAW in St.Louis?LA Knight opened the show just as Roman Reigns arrived in the building. The Megastar spoke about the Bloodline and 946. He then began berating Reigns, leading to the OTC’s entrance. Both men had a heated verbal exchange, and Knight concluded the promo by saying that he would walk out of Money in the Bank as the new World Champion.Bron Breakker & Austin Theory vs. Penta & Je’Von EvansThis was the first match of the night featuring The Vision against Penta and Je’Von Evans in a tag showdown. The Vision attacked Penta as he was making his entrance. The action went back and forth between both teams. In the final moments, Maxxine Dupri distracted the referee, and Logan Paul slid the brass knuckles in the ring. However, instead of Austin Theory, Je’Von Evans grabbed them, knocked him out, and pinned Theory for the victory. Bronson Reed ambushed him and Penta, but Oba Femi came out to their aid.Sol Ruca & Lola Vice vs. Raquel Rodriguez & Roxanne PerezThis was the second tag team match of the night. Both teams held up their own against each other. Toward the end of the bout, Lola Vice accidentally took out her own partner, Sol Ruca, allowing Roxanne Perez to capitalize and score the victory for her team.Ethan Page vs. Rey FenixThe match saw Rey Fenix defend his AAA World Cruiserweight Championship against Ethan Page. Both superstars delivered an instant-classic title bout that kept the audience glued to their seats. In the final moments, Fenix went for the Mexican Muscle Buster, but Page countered it. This led Fenix to utilize the small package and claim the pinfall to win the match.Rey Mysterio & Dragon Lee vs. Dominik Mysterio & JD McDonaghThe tag team bout between both sides was fast-paced bout. It concluded with Big Cass interfering and JD McDonagh using a major headbutt to seal the victory for his team.Becky Lynch vs. Liv MorganThe main event featured Liv Morgan and Becky Lynch clashing in a No.1 contender’s match. It was a highly intense bout with both women fighting for a title shot at Money in the Bank. In the final moments, Stephanie Vaquer came out to the ringside area, but found herself assaulted by both Lynch and Morgan. This agitated her to the point that she attacked them both. articles.title: Panic Time For Yankees? 3 Takeaways From ALDS Game 2 As Rays Go Up 2-0
articles.summary: The Yankees strutted into Tropicana Field talking about their Cy Young-favorite starter and a postseason-ready lineup. They whimpered out of it staring at a 2-0 ALDS hole.
articles.body: The Yankees strutted into Tropicana Field talking about their Cy Young-favorite starter and a postseason-ready lineup. They whimpered out of it staring at a 2-0 ALDS hole. After Tampa Bay ace Drew Rasmussen blanked the Yankees in Game 1, Freddy Peralta and the Rays finished the job in Game 2 with a controlling 5-2 win over New York in Monday’s Game 2. Now the Yankees, who have never truly threatened at any point this series, must win three straight to survive and advance to the ALCS. The Rays are just one win away from advancing to the ALCS for the first time since 2020, when they lost to the Dodgers in the Fall Classic. Here are my takeaways: 1. Not Your Mother’s Rays Perhaps the Yankees weren’t ready for the new Rays, because New York was playing like these were the old Rays. They’re no longer just the scrappy, analytically-forward Rays of old who could be overpowered in a short series. Now, Tampa Bay has legitimate big bats, including Junior Caminero, Jonathan Aranda and Yandy Diaz, to complement their always-excellent pitching depth and clean defense. Both Aranda and Caminero were key to the Rays’ game-opening four-run fifth inning on Monday. Now, the Yankees can no longer afford to make completely avoidable mistakes and be given a runway to overcome them. The Rays, as they have been all year, represent the better team. They showed it through their tighter fundamentals. They showed it through their elite situational baserunning. They showed it with their ability to pounce on multiple moments of weakness from the Yankees. New York committed a total of five errors in Monday’s Game 2. Tampa Bay committed none. The book is out. A team as well-rounded as the Rays has already beat the Yankees on paper. The moment that New York hurts its own chances, the game is over. We can look at an example as recent as the final week of the regular season, when the Rays went to Yankee Stadium for a four-game series in the Bronx. Tampa Bay led 1-0 in the seventh inning with a great-fielding pitcher in Max Fried on the mound. Rays shortstop Taylor Walls pushed a bunt between the mound and first base, no Yankees fielder covered second base, and a run scored from third. Tampa Bay has created a run on that play multiple times this season, manager Kevin Cash said after that game. It’s always impossible to defend. In doing so, the Rays create a wider margin for error before they even take the field for first pitch. Then, throw in their sold-out crowds at Tropicana Field so far in the ALDS, and the Yankees were clearly rattled on Monday. The loud support is there. The talent is there, tenfold. The Rays, finally, seem ready for their moment. After leading the American League in wins all year, all that’s left is the pennant. 2. Yankees’ Tragic First Inning Is All Too Familiar The Yankees committed not one, not two, but three (!) errors in the first inning of Game 2. We’ve seen this clown show too many times to count. The question is, how many times do Yankees officials need to see it before making fundamental changes? All three Yankees errors arrived within the first four batters of Schlittler’s start. The Yankees ace, who is the favorite to win this year’s American League Cy Young award, deserved better. Schlittler himself is battling workload boundaries after blowing past his career-innings high (73) in the first week of June. That he was able to limit the Rays to just one run in the first despite the mistakes of his fielders was nothing short of a miracle. First it was a fielding error by third baseman Ryan McMahon, which allowed Rays designated hitter Yandy Diaz to reach first base with no outs. Aaron Boone considered replacing McMahon at third with infielder Anthony Volpe for Game 2, but the Yankees manager "wanted to prioritize defense." McMahon recorded a career-worst -3 Defensive Runs Saved in 875 innings at third base this year for the Yankees. McMahon’s -3 DRS was ranked 87th out of 130 third basemen who completed at least 800 innings at the hot corner this year. That doesn’t mean Volpe would have been the better option, considering he played just one nine-inning game at third base this season, and that’s it across his major-league career. But choosing to go with McMahon because he’s the better defensive option doesn’t hold much water at this point in the year. In addition to McMahon, second baseman Jazz Chisholm Jr. committed a throwing error, which allowed the Rays to get their first run on the board, and Rays backstop Liam Hicks reached base on catcher interference by Austin Wells. Yankees fans must have gotten flashbacks to Game 5 of the 2024 World Series, when New York lost a championship to the Dodgers by making similar fundamental mistakes and stepping on its own foot. If not for Yankees shortstop George Lombard Jr. stretching his arm to catch another errant throw from Chisholm, the Yankees would have committed four errors in the first inning of Game 2 on Monday. Instead, they settled for three. 3. Where Did The Bronx Bombers Go? After out-scoring the Red Sox 18-2 in their Wild-Card series sweep last week, Yankees bats went cold against the Rays’ dominant pitching in the first two games of the ALDS. New York was understandably silent against Rays ace Drew Rasmussen in Saturday’s Game 1. Rasmussen dominated the Yankees all year, and they had to expect more of the same in the series opener. But the Yankees had their chance to capitalize with a shaky Freddy Peralta on the mound in the fifth inning of Monday’s Game 2, and they failed to come through. Peralta was sweating after giving up a double to Austin Wells on two outs in the fifth. (It’s noteworthy that Wells smartly stopped at second base after trying and failing to leg out a triple on a similar ball he put in play in Game 1.) Peralta was clearly shaken up, as he walked McMahon, the Yankees No. 9 hitter, on six pitches in the next at-bat. The Rays pulled Peralta after that, with Tampa Bay’s trade-deadline acquisition completing just 4 ⅔ innings on 66 pitches. They went to their bullpen for Yankees designated hitter Ben Rice, who drew a walk against left-hander Cam Booser. Then, with the bases loaded, and the Yankees tied with the Rays 1-1, Yankees left fielder Cody Bellinger flew out to center for the final out of the fifth inning. New York’s offensive threat, hard to come by against an elite Rays pitching staff, never materialized again. Besides Rice, who homered twice and went 2-for-3 with a walk in Game 2, the rest of the Yankees offense was completely befuddled by the four Tampa Bay arms who stepped on the mound on Monday. After losing Game 1 at Tropicana Field, ALDS Game 2 with an unreliable Peralta and an ace in Schlittler on the mound was a must-win for the Yankees. It’s difficult for even the most optimistic of Yankees fans to believe they can turn the best-of-five series around after being down 2-0 – with their best player in Aaron Judge nursing a calf strain on the bench, absent from the active roster. 3 ½. What’s Next? Yankees left-hander Max Fried (5-5, 2.80 ERA, 104 strikeouts) will take the hill for Game 3 on Wednesday at Yankee Stadium — as long as he’s available. Fried’s girlfriend is due to give birth sometime this week, which could put his availability into question for the ALDS. If Fried is unable to make his outing, the Yankees will start southpaw Carlos Rodon in his place. As of Monday night, the Rays had not announced a starter for Game 3.

articles.title: Major triple-threat title match set for WWE Money in the Bank 2026
articles.summary: WWE Money in the Bank 2026 Premium Live Event is just days away, and a huge showdown has been made official.
articles.body: WWE Money in the Bank 2026 Premium Live Event is just days away, and a huge showdown has been made official. It will feature three competitors from the women's division battling it out in a high-stakes match, and only one will leave as the new champion.WWE Money in the Bank 2026 will feature a major Women's title matchThe October 5 episode of Monday Night RAW featured a blockbuster main event match between Becky Lynch and Liv Morgan. The match was to determine the No.1 contender to Stephanie Vaquer's WWE Women's World Championship at Money in the Bank 2026. This came off the heels of a feud brewing between the three women ever since Vaquer and Lynch returned to WWE on RAW after SummerSlam, after their respective hiatuses.The match was nothing short of heated, with tensions between Morgan and Lynch, who are longtime rivals themselves. Both women came hitting with their best moves from their respective arsenals. Yet neither was ready to give up that easily, with a huge title opportunity at stake. Overall, it was a highly exhilarating bout worthy of the main event of Monday Night RAW. However, the interesting turn came towards the end of the bout.Stephanie Vaquer came out to neutralize the threat of Morgan's allies, the Judgment Day, and then stood on the apron. This saw Becky Lynch accidentally take out Vaquer. Following that, Morgan attacked Vaquer and then turned her focus on Lynch. As they continued to trade blows, La Primera came back in the ring and attacked them both at the same time, ending the match in a double DQ. She then inflicted a major beatdown on both competitors, leading to the arrival of RAW GM Adam Pearce to control the situation.In a surprising turn of events, Vaquer demanded to face both Morgan and Lynch with her Women's World title on the line. The crowd came unglued, and Pearce made it official for Money in the Bank 2026. While it is commendable for Stephanie Vaquer to take on a tough challenge for her title, her chances of retaining it are slim now. articles.title: Hello, Atlanta, Michael Penix & Bijan Robinson: 3 Takeaways From Falcons Win vs. Saints
articles.summary: All of a sudden, the Falcons appear to have one of the best offenses in the NFL. Here are our takeaways from their win over the Saints.
articles.body: Superdome (New Orleans) — After a very ugly opening two weeks of the season, the Atlanta Falcons are quickly back at .500, while the New Orleans Saints keep digging themselves into holes they can't climb out of. The Falcons improved to 2-2 on the season with their decisive 45-24 win over the Saints in New Orleans on Monday night, but what's more noteworthy is that Atlanta is now 2-0 with Michael Penix Jr. at quarterback this season. For the second straight week, Penix quarterbacked the Falcons to a dominant win in primetime as Atlanta has firmly placed itself in the race to win the NFC South. Here are my three takeaways from Monday night's game. 1.Falcons Have Been Dominant With Michael Penix In the previous six seasons, the Falcons didn’t have a single road win by 20 points or more. Now they’ve done it twice in the last 11 days. First with a 34-10 win over the Packers at Lambeau Field, and on Monday night with an equally impressive win over the Saints, the Falcons have shown an ability to separate from opponents that they’ve lacked for a long time. The two routs coincide with the healthy return of quarterback Michael Penix. Obviously, the star of the offense is running back Bijan Robinson, but that wasn’t enough in two ugly losses with backup Cooper Rush at quarterback. But in two starts, Penix has taken advantage of defenses trying to contain Robinson — an efficient 18 of 25 for 256 yards against the Packers, and 15 of 20 for 223 yards and a touchdown in beating the Saints. His passer rating of 127.7 is a career-best, too, as the Saints' 45 points were the most they've put up in a game in 10 years. It’s a strong reflection on new offensive coordinator Tommy Rees, who came to Atlanta with Kevin Stefanski and was entrusted with the offensive play-calling. The Falcons rotate Robinson with backup Brian Robinson, who had three touchdowns of his own Monday, keeping fresh legs late in the game for both backs. Atlanta is home for its next three games, but they’re doozies. They take on the Ravens, Bears and 49ers, who are a combined 10-2 this season, so even one win in three would be impressive. Nobody is running away with the NFC South, but the Falcons need to keep up with the 2-2 Panthers, who routed them in Week 2 before Penix was playing. 2.What If The Saints Didn’t Dig A Deep Hole In Every Game? Even without first-round pick wide receiver Jordyn Tyson, who’s been out with injury, the Saints have a top-10 offense in scoring and yardage. And yet they’re 1-3, thanks to an inability to start games well on either side of the ball. Four games in, the Saints had double-digit deficits in three of those games — down 21-0 to the Lions in a one-point loss, down 14-3 to the Ravens in their lone win, down 13-6 to the Raiders in another close loss, and routed 24-7 in the first half Monday night against the Falcons. They missed running back Travis Etienne against Atlanta, and he’ll miss at least three more games with his hamstring injury. The Falcons have Bijan Robinson, and the Saints don't. So, the first-half rushing advantage for Atlanta was 138-15. Yikes! When the Saints rebounded from a 1-8 start last year, their defense gave up 17.5 points per game in the final eight games, leading them to a 5-3 finish. But in 2026, they were giving up 27 points per game in their first three, and the Falcons only raised that average Monday night. They’re a bottom-10 defense against the run and on third downs. Until that changes, the offense will throw the ball a lot in the second half and look like a better offense than they really are. 3.Falcons Need To Find A Pass Rush To Beat Better Teams The fear going into the year was that the season-ending injury loss of Jalon Walker and the eight-game suspension for James Pearce would leave the Falcons without any real pass rush in the first half of the season. That’s basically played out so far. After finishing second in the NFL with 57 sacks last year, the Falcons have just seven in four games, on pace for just more than half as many as last season. They’d gotten 2.5 sacks from Za’Darius Smith, who came out of retirement, but he missed much of Monday’s game with a concussion, so his immediate future is uncertain. If they’re going to have a chance in these next three home games — all against teams in the top eight of our power rankings entering Week 4 — they need to be able to get in the backfield and disrupt even the backup quarterbacks they might end up facing. Pearce can be a boost in the second half of the season, but the lack of pass rush is part of why the Falcons' defense has just two takeaways in four games, matching the NFL low. Not sure who the help is coming from, but it’s the missing piece right now to make Atlanta better than just a good offensive team.

articles.title: Luka Doncic scores 21 as Lakers unveil new defense in preseason win over Kings
articles.summary: Lakers star Luka Doncic puts on a show with Walker Kessler and Austin Reaves sidelined by injury in a 127-103 preseason win over the Sacramento Kings.
articles.body:
The Lakers pressed, switched and swarmed from the opening whistle. After the Sacramento Kings were caught for a shot-clock violation on the first possession of Monday's preseason game, Luka Doncic raised his fists toward the Lakers bench with a triumphant grin to symbolize the successful start.

But Doncic's smile toward his teammates had a hint of sarcasm; this is still just an exhibition.

The Lakers teased their new defensive identity in a 127-103 preseason win against the Sacramento Kings on Monday at Golden 1 Center, rolling out their deep group of wings to overcome a short-handed bench.

Playing without star center Walker Kessler , who missed the game with a finger injury, and guard Austin Reaves (ankle), Doncic led the Lakers with 21 points. He took a hard knee to the side of his quad midway through the second quarter, but stayed in the game. With the Lakers up 26 points at halftime, Doncic didn't need to return.

"We all had fun out there," said Doncic, who relished the chance to play in his first competitive basketball game in six months, one of the longest breaks of his career. "Especially with Matisse [Thybulle] and Ziaire [Williams], just that beginning of the game, the start, that's contagious for everybody, and how they start the game, it was inspirational."

The star guard actually was bringing down the team's shooting average. While he was three-for-nine from three-point range in the first half, his teammates combined to make nine of their first 13 three-pointers. Williams led with perfect three-for-three shooting from distance with 13 points and one steal while serving as the Lakers' top on-ball defender. Thybulle, another key defensive offseason addition, had two steals and made two threes.

At halftime, coaches showed players a clip of Williams, a 6-foot-9 forward who signed on a minimum contract, guarding the ball full court. The highlight then showed how Doncic's energy picked up. Thybulle followed suit.

"You don't wanna be the only guy out there that's not being physical, not picking up full, not being a pest," Williams said. "Coming in, I knew that I saw that the team could use that, someone who could pick up full and could guard the main ball handler and really set the tone on that end. I try to just focus on that every possession."

Coach JJ Redick, in his third season with the Lakers, said it was the first time in his tenure that he felt the team had multiple players who were capable of handling that defensive responsibility. The Lakers call it their "line of confrontation." Williams, Thybulle, second-year forward Adou Thiero and guard Quentin Grimes were among the players who guarded the ball full court. The Lakers forced four steals in the first quarter and 15 for the game. They averaged 8.5 per game last season.

The product Monday is far from what the Lakers hope to show in their regular-season opener Oct. 21 against the Golden State Warriors.

Kessler was wearing a splint on his left pinky finger after he jammed it on the backboard during practice last week. Redick doesn't expect any of the injuries that kept Reaves, guard Collin Sexton (lower body) and two-way forward Arthur Kaluma (lower body) to be long-term.

Reaves, who tweaked his ankle in practice, still went through his pregame warmup routine Monday.

Even without two of their three top players, the Lakers overwhelmed the Kings, who are expected to be among the worst teams in the Western Conference again. Rookie point guard Darius Acuff, the No. 7 pick in last April's draft, had 19 points with four assists and five turnovers.

This story originally appeared in Los Angeles Times .

articles.title: Calha is ready 💪, Amorim woes and Spalletti's XI: morning news☀️
articles.summary: Last night's fine win over Turkey brings the international break for Italy and the other national teams to a close, after domestic leagues were put on hold....
articles.body:
Last night's fine win over Turkey brings the international break for Italy and the other national teams to a close, after domestic leagues were put on hold. Serie A returns on Saturday.

The top clubs will therefore be back in action very soon. Let's take a look at this morning's biggest stories.

Juventus want to get their push for the top spots back on track straight away and are not underestimating their trip to Cagliari , currently fourth in the table. After a three-week break, Spalletti is expected to rely on his regular starters and the players who stayed at Continassa, including Bremer, McKennie and Kolo Muani. According to La Gazzetta dello Sport , the aim is to avoid another slip-up in Sardinia and make the best possible start to a busy October, with seven matches in around twenty days across the league and Europa League.

In defence, Spalletti will build around Bremer , alongside Kalulu and Lucumí, while McKennie is expected to return to the starting line-up. Up front, Kolo Muani is set to keep his place, still searching for his first Serie A goal of 2026, with Conceiçao favoured over Zhegrova after returning from international duty with Portugal. The Kosovan, who scored a goal and provided an assist for his national team, is nevertheless an important option off the bench. Juve want to start strongly: after beating Atalanta, the Bianconeri are three points off the top.

🚑 Milan, injuries force a reshuffle for the Rossoneri

Milan have lost two important players on the flanks. Their first serious injury setback of the season concerns Alexis Saelemaekers , who will need surgery on his right ankle and could be out for at least four months. Further complicating Ruben Amorim 's plans is the injury to Pervis Estupinan , who suffered a knee problem while playing for Ecuador. According to La Gazzetta dello Sport , the coach will therefore have to rethink both flanks, starting with the match against Sassuolo .

On the left, the most natural solution is Bartesaghi , while Amorim could turn to the in-form Diego Moreira to replace Saelemaekers, or consider more cautious alternatives such as playing Rabiot out wide or returning to a 3-4-2-1. The Belgian had become an important part of the Rossoneri's new system, and his absence will force the coach to find a different balance just as a run of seven matches in twenty days begins.

Inter's playmaking duties are returning to Hakan Calhanoglu . The Turkish midfielder has trained with the squad for the first time since his latest adductor problem and is now aiming to be available for the match against Parma . According to La Gazzetta dello Sport , Chivu will have a week to assess his fitness and decide how much to use him in the league and Champions League.

His recovery also comes at a delicate time for the player's future, with his contract expiring in June 2027 . His performances and, above all, his ability to stay fit will also be crucial to any renewal, with Inter needing to assess the terms of a potential new deal. In the meantime, Zielinski remains the main alternative in the playmaker role and has already deputised for Calhanoglu in recent matches. Now, however, the Turk wants to put his injury problems behind him and reclaim his place at the heart of Inter's midfield.

Aurelio De Laurentiis has returned to Castel Volturno to take stock of Napoli 's current situation, with particular attention to their injured players. The president met with Massimiliano Allegri and sporting director Giovanni Manna, while according to CalcioNapoli24 , one of the priorities is to gain a better understanding of the injury problems that have been affecting the team for several weeks.

Saturday's match against Frosinone is also a key focus, seen as crucial to getting the Azzurri back on track after a difficult start. De Laurentiis wants answers and greater consistency, while Allegri's staff await the return of several players: Meret, Spinazzola and Marianucci are close to rejoining the squad, while McTominay and Anguissa's fitness still needs to be assessed.

Roma have returned to training at Trigoria ahead of their trip to Como, the first fixture in a long, gruelling run. The main doubt concerns Bryan Cristante , who is dealing with inflammation of a collateral knee ligament. "He's receiving treatment; it takes time," Gasperini told Sky Sport , suggesting that no risks will be taken, with the match against Real Madrid also on the horizon.

According to La Gazzetta dello Sport , Cristante is therefore expected to start on the bench at Como, with de Roon ready to make his first start in a Roma shirt. The Dutchman is expected to partner Koné in midfield, in a match with special significance for the former Atalanta player, who will immediately be reunited with familiar surroundings. For Gasperini, meanwhile, it will mark the start of a run of nine matches in 27 days .

Lazio continue to monitor their injury list ahead of the league's return. Cancellieri , who has been dealing with a cut to his knee that required stitches, is aiming to rejoin the squad, and there is optimism over his availability for the match against Monza . Dele-Bashiru and Marusic , both on the road to recovery, have the same target. According to Corriere dello Sport , Rovella , sidelined since 30 August with a calf injury, will also try to speed up his return.

The timeline is less certain for Cataldi , who is dealing with quadriceps fatigue: the midfielder could target the match against Juventus on 18 October, but there are no guarantees. Gudmundsson , however, will be unavailable, still sidelined after dislocating his right shoulder. Lazio therefore hope to recover at least some of their absent players for their next league fixture.

🤑 Fiorentina must sell before moving for Tiago Gabriel

Tiago Gabriel is one of the names linked with Fiorentina ahead of the January transfer window. The Lecce defender has attracted interest from several clubs, including Sporting Lisbon , and is valued at close to €30 million . According to La Nazione , a fee of that size would make an immediate signing difficult, but Fabio Paratici could work with agent Jorge Mendes on a deal structure that would defer part of the payment.

The move would, however, depend on the future of Marin Pongracic . Before making a serious move for the Lecce centre-back, Fiorentina would first need to find a new club for the Croatian and bring in a substantial fee from his sale. Only then would the Viola have the financial room to try to bring Tiago Gabriel to Florence.

articles.title: Watch Luka Doncic moment in Los Angeles Lakers game which could be a major concern
articles.summary: Luka Doncic looked like he was on another level in the first half against the Sacramento Kings, but one moment towards the end will lead to fans worrying. Th...
articles.body:
Luka Doncic looked like he was on another level in the first half against the Sacramento Kings, but one moment towards the end will lead to fans worrying.

The Los Angeles Lakers destroyed the Sacramento Kings 127-100 in their preseason clash. Luka Doncic led the way, scoring 21 points in 16 first-half minutes. His performance included back-to-back three pointers, and gave fans plenty of reasons to be excited.

It is a big season for Doncic. He is officially the main man in LA after LeBron James' departure, and he needs to live up to that responsibility. While his actual play showed that he is ready, there was a moment in the clash which showed that his body might not be.

Luka Doncic was seen limping on the court in the final minutes of the first half

The Slovenian superstar was done for the evening at the half. The Lakers essentially emptied their bench for the second part of the game. Leaving Doncic in for longer would have almost seemed unfair to the Kings. He was helping the Lakers casually run up the score in the second quarter.

While the takeaways from his performance were all largely positive, there was one hiccup right at the end. In recent years, Luka has become a bit injury-prone. As the first half came to an end, he was spotted limping quite heavily, which is certainly concerning for fans of the team.

Luka is now in his prime on arguably the NBA's biggest franchise. The clock is ticking for him to get some major accolades before people start losing faith in his ability to maximise his generational talent. Health is the only thing which is likely to stop him, making this a problem.

Doncic has hobbled on the court various times in the past. Anyone who watches him knows that Luka often looks banged up when he plays. Lakers fans will certainly be hoping it was just a painful hit and nothing more. If he does get injured for whatever reason, it will be the end of the Lakers' aspirations this year.

Franchise legend Alvin Kamara looked like his vintage self but left with a knee injury on a night when legendary former Saints special teams hero Steve Gleason watched alongside Peyton and Eli Manning.

Gleason, who has a statue outside of the Caesars Superdome, had jokes for the legendary NFL brothers including one on the enormous size of Peyton Manning 's forehead.

"Steve, how easy would it have been to block Peyton as a punter?" Eli Manning asked the former Saints punt blocker extraordinaire alongside football of his brother Peyton Manning attempting to coffin corner punt.

"Peyton, unfortunately for both of us, long before I'd hit the ball, I'd hit your forehead," Gleason said, drawing laughter from the Manning duo.

Gleason blocked a punt in September 2006 against the Falcons in the Louisiana Superdome's 'Rebirth Game,' its first since Hurricane Katrina struck the area. Gleason got a statue for his efforts as the play became a symbol of hope and rebirth for a city that was put through hell during the Category 3-5 hurricane. Manning is the son of Saints legend Archie Manning who has been known to take jokes about his appearance in stride.

The Saints Monday Night football loss caused coach Kellen Moore's team to drop to 1-3 while fans breathed a sigh of relief over news on Chris Olave's injury scare . Kamara had a night that was frustrating but also special as he thrilled fans with his pair of TD scores.

Gleason didn't get to watch the Saints get a much needed win, but he did have fun calling the game with two legendary former players. The Saints have a long way to go to match the Manning brothers' feats during their playing days, but will have another opportunity to move forward in their October 11 game at Minnesota.

DAVE ROBERTS: Yeah, this is one of those things that I'm gonna continue to give Andy leash. I believe in him. I feel that for us to win the World Series this year, we're gonna need him to be an active part of our team.

And so I hope it doesn't get to that point. We're not there yet.

DAVE ROBERTS: I think there's trying to do too much. I think that clearly when he came back he was swinging the bat really well, had success and then I think there's a little bit of trying too much, yeah.

articles.title: Saints’ Kellen Moore is still trying to figure out solution to New Orleans’ slow starts
articles.summary: The New Orleans Saints are running out of patience and answers. After Monday night’s humiliating 45-24 loss to the Atlanta Falcons dropped New Orleans to 1-3...
articles.body:
The New Orleans Saints are running out of patience and answers. After Monday night's humiliating 45-24 loss to the Atlanta Falcons dropped New Orleans to 1-3, head coach Kellen Moore admitted that his team's recurring slow starts remain an unresolved problem. It continues to put the Saints in difficult positions before their offense can find its rhythm.

"Yeah, it's just this point. Again, obviously not coaching it well enough, not executing it well enough," Moore said postgame. "They came out, went right down the field, scored, we went three and out. And we didn't score until the second quarter. We've tried a number of different things. And obviously we haven't solved this, but we gotta find a way."

Atlanta immediately exposed the problem Monday . The Falcons marched down the field for an opening touchdown before New Orleans answered with a three-and-out. Those early deficits have become particularly damaging with Travis Etienne Jr sidelined by injury. This has forced Tyler Shough and the passing game to shoulder more responsibility while the defense struggles to contain opposing rushing attacks.

New Orleans opened 2026 with a 31-30 loss to Detroit before beating Baltimore 24-17. Since then, losses to the Raiders and Falcons have exposed growing issues. Atlanta ran for more than 200 yards and scored five rushing touchdowns. That underscored the defensive concerns facing Moore's team.

The Saints now travel to Minnesota for Week 5 with little margin for error. Moore and his staff have tried multiple approaches to improve their opening sequences. However, the results remain unchanged. Until New Orleans finds a way to start games with urgency, its season could unravel before halftime becomes relevant.

articles.title: Commanders quarterback update: Latest on Jayden Daniels and Marcus Mariota
articles.summary: Commanders provide updates on Jayden Daniels' return and Marcus Mariota's injury.
articles.body:
After the Washington Commanders ' Week 4 loss to the Indianapolis Colts in London, head coach Dan Quinn updated everyone on injured backup quarterback Marcus Mariota.

"The team thinks it's an MCL injury," Quinn said. "When we get the scan tomorrow, we'll have further knowledge of what we're dealing with and length and all those."

Mariota was injured on Washington's second drive in the first quarter after he was sacked and a defender landed on his leg. The injury looked scary and potentially season-ending. However, on Monday, Quinn provided more context on Mariota's injury, confirming it was a sprained MCL, the same injury he suffered in the first preseason game.

"Marcus sprained his MCL," Quinn said on Monday. "It's the same one that he injured in training camp. Don't have an exact timetable yet. We'll know a little bit more after his return-to-play process, but he'll be working off to the side as it goes through the next week or so."

That's terrific news for Mariota and the Commanders, considering it appeared much worse. Mariota missed around three weeks this summer with the same injury. Obviously, that doesn't mean this one follows on the exact same timeline, but barring setbacks, it should be close. Washington plays the New York Giants and San Francisco 49ers over the next two weeks before its Week 7 bye, which could line up Mariota for a Week 8 return.

As for starting quarterback Jayden Daniels, he'll return to practice on Wednesday, as expected, and take all the reps.

"Yeah, the goal is for him to have a full week of practice, full week, and start on Sunday," Quinn said.

No mystery there. Daniels will be in the lineup next week, three weeks after dislocating his left (non-throwing) elbow in Week 2 at Dallas. It's the same elbow that Daniels dislocated last November.

Daniels returning for Week 5 was already the plan. This isn't the Commanders panicking about possibly having to start rookie Athan Kaliakmanis against the Giants. Daniels was in London with the team last week, in his brace, to get some practice time before a full return this week.

It's certainly been a tough year for Washington on the injury front, especially at quarterback, but all things considered, the Commanders have been fortunate with Daniels and Mariota.

articles.title: Will Cristiano Ronaldo play for Portugal after a row with coach Jesus?
articles.summary: Ronaldo sparked controversy last week when he walked out of the camp after learning that he would not start a game.
articles.body:
The drama surrounding Cristiano Ronaldo’s international future took another turn after Portugal head coach Jorge Jesus left the door open for the 41-year-old superstar’s return following his abrupt departure from the national team’s training camp.

The sentiment is shared by the Portuguese Football Federation president Pedro ⁠⁠Proenca, who believes the episode is a mere misunderstanding that could be resolved internally.

But how did the apparent rift start, and will Ronaldo ever play again for Portugal?

What happened between Ronaldo and Jesus?

Ronaldo left the Portugal squad late on Wednesday, shortly after the head coach’s news conference, where Jesus confirmed that the five-time Ballon d’Or winner would be left out of his starting lineup for the match against Denmark, marking a second consecutive Nations League game absence.

Ronaldo’s decision to walk out came as a shock, as he had been due to train with his teammates at the Parken Stadium in Copenhagen.

Portugal’s leading scorer had already spent the entirety of the 2-1 Nations League win away to Norway on September 27 on the bench, having captained the side in the 1-0 home victory over Wales three days before.

The game in Oslo was the first time since November 2024 that Ronaldo had not featured for Portugal despite not being injured or suspended.

Ronaldo appeared to indicate that the reasons behind Jesus’s decision to bench him ran deeper and hinted at a departure from the national team he has graced for more than two decades.

“In due course, I will tell the truth to all the Portuguese people about my reasons for leaving the national team, to which I have always been dedicated,” Ronaldo said in a cryptic Instagram post, announcing his sudden exit from the camp.

Spanish sports daily Marca said Jesus and Proenca followed Ronaldo to Copenhagen airport in an attempt to persuade him to stay with the squad, before the player boarded his private jet.

There were reports that Portuguese Prime Minister Luis Montenegro had even discussed the issue of Ronaldo’s involvement with the coach on Wednesday.

Jesus insisted that there was no rift between them, although the 72-year-old, who was appointed in July, acknowledged that his captain was disappointed to remain on the bench against Norway.

Despite his absence, Nations League title holders Portugal won, defeating Denmark 4-2 in Copenhagen and Norway 2-1 in Porto. They also became the first team to qualify for the quarterfinals, ensuring a top-two finish in Group A4.

Forward Goncalo Ramos stepped up in Ronaldo’s absence, scoring three goals to be the team’s joint top scorer along with Joao Felix, while the AC Milan player also bagged an assist.

What did Portugal’s coach say about Ronaldo?

On Sunday, coach Jesus said Ronaldo could return to the national team ⁠⁠if he chooses ⁠⁠to.

“If he wants to, he’ll return to the national team. We can talk before the next call-up, but Cris is the one who’s going ‌‌to decide,” said Jesus, who also coached Ronaldo at Saudi Arabian club Al-Nassr.

“He’s the one who should decide how he wants to end his time with the national team. In my first call-up, I said, ‘I need you, I need you to be close to me, playing or not playing, I need you’. And now I’m saying ⁠⁠the same thing.”

Jesus expects the forward to be available for the next international window if he wants to return.

What have the Portugal players said about Ronaldo?

Midfielder Bruno Fernandes said on Saturday he had spoken to Ronaldo and dismissed suggestions of a rift within Portugal’s squad.

“I had a chat with him and what I said to him is ‌‌what I’ll repeat here: the most important thing is that, whatever happens, Cristiano Ronaldo will never cease to be the greatest symbol of our national team, of our football and of the country,” Fernandes told a news conference.

“For what he has achieved not only in Portugal, but all over the world. He has a place reserved not only amongst the all-time greats, but also in the hearts of all Portuguese people.”

“The most important thing is that we ⁠⁠stop stirring up trouble; there are no divisions within the national team. It is ⁠⁠one team and will remain so, despite any noise that may come from outside.”

Fernandes called for unity after a tumultuous few days in which Portugal fans’ opinions have been split over Ronaldo’s decision.

“We are outside of this controversy, but what I ask is that the country does not divide itself, does not make choices, that it respects all sides, but, at the same time, Cris is and will be the biggest icon of our national team. He deserves everyone’s respect, regardless of who likes him more or [who likes him] less,” Fernandes added.

When was Ronaldo’s last match for Portugal and how did he perform?

Ronaldo featured just once for Portugal during this year’s Nations League, playing 67 minutes in their 1-0 home win over Wales.

It was a frustrating night for the Al-Nassr forward, who misfired several times . He found the side netting once and shinned an inviting volley high over from close range.

Around the hour mark, Ronaldo slid the ball into the Wales net but, to his evident disbelief, was ruled offside.

He was still shaking his head when Jesus substituted him seven minutes later.

Ronaldo, who made his Portugal debut in 2003 at the age of 18, has said this will “probably” be his final year in football. The forward has been a fixture of the national team for more than two decades and has played at six World Cups.

Former Real Madrid and Manchester United attacker Ronaldo is ⁠⁠Portugal’s record scorer and most-capped player, with 146 goals in 234 international appearances.

He reached the World Cup semifinals in 2006 and captained his country to glory at Euro 2016. Ronaldo and Portugal were eliminated by eventual winners Spain in the last 16 of this year’s World Cup.

Portugal have completed their quota of four Nations League fixtures in this extended international window.

Their upcoming matches are in the next window: a home game with Norway on November 14 and an away match against Wales three days later.

Those matches will wrap up Portugal’s league phase in the Nations League, which they have won twice.
