articles.title: Gauff in racial abuse controversy at China Open after replayed point
articles.summary: Coco Gauff was targeted online after stopping play during a crucial point in the first set against China’s Sun Xinran.
articles.body:
Coco Gauff says she has received an “insane” amount of racial abuse on social media after the two-time Grand Slam champion beat local teenager Sun Xinran at the China Open in a third-round match, where a replayed point prompted an online backlash.

The American tennis star won 7-5, 6-1 to reach the fourth round, but was targeted after stopping play during a crucial point in the first set, raising her hand to complain about a flickering advertising board just as Sun was about to put away a winner.

After a video review, the umpire ordered a replay. Gauff won the replayed point and held serve for 5-5 before cruising to victory against the 16-year-old Chinese.

Gauff said she had received a barrage of abusive messages on social media after the match.

“You can dislike me or disagree about what happened without being racist,” Gauff, who is Black, said on X early on Tuesday in reply to a post containing a racial slur.

“The amount of racist comments/direct messages I’ve received in the last few hours is insane.

The WTA has made efforts to tackle the issue of online abuse by introducing an AI-powered system which monitors thousands of players and officials on social media.

A study by the WTA and World Tennis showed players were subjected to more than 12,000 abusive posts and messages on social media in 2025, up from 8,000 posts a year earlier.

Gauff also explained that she was following the rules when she challenged the point. Players are allowed to request video reviews of select judgement calls, including claims a distraction may have interfered with play.

The 22-year-old said she had spoken to Sun about the point at the end of the match.

“Xinran’s an incredible talent and player, I apologised for the situation at the end of the match and she completely understood,” she wrote.

“I didn’t like to see her so emotional as I’ve been there and I really understand what it’s like but this is the beginning of an incredible career. It was an honour to share the court in front of her home crowd.”

Un ecosistema en el que en los últimos cinco años han irrumpido competiciones emergentes, como Kings League, Hexagon Cup o Unrivaled, que han cambiado el formato tradicional y han conseguido atraer a marcas de gran consumo desde la primera edición. Pero, ¿qué tienen estos eventos que se han convertido en el place to be de marcas de gran consumo como Cupra, Generali o Sephora? “La Generali Hexagon Cup está contribuyendo a redefinir cómo se vive y se consume el pádel. No se limita a reproducir los modelos tradicionales, sino que aporta nuevas formas de conectar el deporte con los aficionados”, resume María Babé Ayuso, chief marketing & customer officer de Generali España, marca que da nombre a la competición de pádel por equipos. Hexagon Cup, Kings y Queens League o Unrivaled tienen algo en común: cuentan con estructuras operativas centralizadas, formatos adaptados al consumo ágil y de corta duración, reglas diseñadas para maximizar el interés de un público al que le cuesta más que antaño mantener la atención, y una capacidad inédita para monetizar la audiencia propia de sus streamers y embajadores. Quienes impulsan clubes y competiciones son celebridades, deportistas retirados o en activo y creadores de contenido que son un gran altavoz mediático, y en muchos casos, sitúan sobre el terreno de juego a verdaderas estrellas del deporte. Por ejemplo, Paige Bueckers, estrella emergente de la WNBA, debutó con Unrivaled cuando ya era una celebridad del baloncesto universitario en Estados Unidos. La liga de baloncesto femenino 3x3 firmó con ella un acuerdo por el que la jugadora sería inversora y embajadora, además de jugadora durante una temporada. Hoy, la competición suma casi 700.000 seguidores entre Instagram y TikTok. La Kings League y la Queens League se apoyan en una cartera de más de veinte creadores de contenido que presiden sus clubes y crean contenido jornada tras jornada. Hexagon Cup, por su parte, cuenta con Rafa Nadal o Eva Longoria entre los impulsores de sus equipos. Habría que tirar la mirada atrás, a 2017, para encontrar uno de los primeros precedentes de proyectos disruptivos impulsados por deportistas: la Laver Cup de Roger Federer. En su día fue un revulsivo del calendario tenístico por plantear un formato de torneo diferente que convenció a las mejores raquetas del calendario. No competían de manera individual como el público estaba acostumbrado, sino que Europa se medía a los mejores del resto del mundo, mediante un sistema de puntuación dinámico que hacía mantener la emoción. Todo ello, acompañado de leyendas del tenis en los banquillos. El nivel competitivo y las virales reacciones de los tenistas durante los partidos ha convertido este evento en uno de los momentos más esperados del año tenístico. Hoy, las competiciones emergentes abrazan lo viral, y las marcas lo agradecen. “Los presidentes son una parte esencial de la Kings League; cada uno aporta su comunidad, la conversación no empieza ni termina con el partido: hay contenido, rivalidades y reacciones durante toda la semana. Las marcas pueden entrar en esas historias de forma muy natural y amplificar su impacto en las redes y en los canales de presidentes”, afirma Álvaro Abati, director comercial de la Kings League. Se trata de un ecosistema compuesto por competiciones en España, Francia, Italia, Alemania, Brasil, México..., que, sumado a todos los clubes participantes, englobaron un total de 126 acuerdos de patrocinio a través de 83 patrocinadores a principios de 2026, según datos extraídos de Intelligence 2P, la unidad de estrategia e inteligencia de mercado de 2Playbook. Mientras que Adidas viste a los clubes de todas las ligas masculinas, Cupra explota el naming del pabellón en España y Alemania; Fonzies el de Italia y Trident el de Brasil. En México Openbank da nombre a la competición. Solo en España, la temporada 2025-2026 acumuló más de 600 millones de visualizaciones en directo a través de sus retransmisiones, un dato que refuerza la apuesta por formatos capaces de generar consumo en vivo y recorrido posterior en clips. Son resultados fruto del fuerte grado de interacción con el público. “La marca puede formar parte del show; En la Kings League siempre están pasando cosas: las Secret Cards, el dado, el MVP, el gol doble… Son momentos propios de nuestra competición que generan contenido y conversación, y que una marca puede hacer suyos”, añade Abati. Hexagon Cup también ha buscado aportar algo nuevo al mundo del pádel. Debutó en 2024 en Madrid y lleva tres ediciones a sus espaldas que le han bastado para dar el salto internacional y contar con más eventos en le extranjero. “Nosotros no nos incorporamos únicamente como patrocinador, sino como socio de una competición con la que podemos construir experiencias relevantes para los aficionados y acompañar la expansión de un deporte que cada vez llega a más personas y a más mercados”, asegura la directora de marketing de Generali España. En otras palabras: que sea una disciplina cada vez más practicada ha sido clave para que la empresa se decidiera a dar nombre a la competición. No es la única: también se han incorporado al pool de patrocinadorse la automovilística Omoda; lo marca de electrónica de audio JBL o la cervecera Mahou, que lleva apoyando el evento desde los orígenes, cuando los primeros nombres de celebridades saltaron a la palestra como propietarios de los equipos. “Son una parte muy importante del ecosistema, pero intentamos que su participación tenga sentido dentro de cada colaboración”, reconoce Astrid Thams commercial managing director de Hexagon World Series. Entre las celebridades que cuentan con equipos está Leo Messi junto a Kun Agüero, también vinculado al universo Kings League, pero también Andy Murray y Robert Lewandowski, además de Nadal y Eva Longoria. Thams asegura que las marcas se vinculan al torneo no sólo por dicha cartera de celebridades, sino porque “el pádel está en crecimiento y tiene una audiencia cada vez más internacional”. “Los partners valoran la posibilidad de crecer con nosotros y llevar esa relación a nuevos mercados con la Hexagon World Series”, afirma. Tras cada evento, piden feedback a las marcas, que “valoran la capacidad de aprovechar el evento desde diferentes ángulos”, describe. Desde tener presencia en la pista a desarrollar una activación en el recinto que permita interactuar con los fans, pasando por generar contenido desde el evento o crear experiencias específicas vinculadas a sus productos y servicios. “Son capas diferentes de una misma asociación que permiten trabajar tanto notoriedad como engagement”, afirma. Pero ¿qué opinan las marcas? Playtomic, que es patrocinador de Hexagon Cup, destaca que apoyar una competición así aporta “capacidad para generar nuevas formas de conectar con el público, atraer nuevas audiencias y llevar el pádel más allá de lo que sucede únicamente dentro de la pista”, afirma Laura Rivas, head of sponsorships de la plataforma. Generali subraya que “la combinación de competición y entretenimiento generan una experiencia atractiva para públicos muy diversos y acercan este deporte a nuevas audiencias”. A ello se suma el poder activar en directo durante la cita y “relacionarnos de una forma más directa con clientes, mediadores y empleados en un entorno positivo y relevante para ellos”, añade María Babé. Eso sí, no todos los nuevos proyectos sobreviven, y el claro ejemplo ha sido LIV Golf. Surgió como competición disruptiva que iba a disputar la hegemonía a los circuitos tradicionales de golf, y cinco años después está en bancarrota tras no conseguir suficiente apoyo de las marcas e inversores. Kings League, Unrivaled o Hexagon Cup no han surgido para amenazar la hegemonía a las competiciones hegemónicas, sino como complemento. En algunos casos, incluso se alían con los órganos rectores de su deporte, como ocurre con la Hexagon Cup, competición que sigue las normas que fija la Federación Internacional de Pádel (FIP).

articles.title: Harmanpreet Kaur steps down as captain of India’s women’s cricket team
articles.summary: The 37-year-old is longest-serving cricket captain, among both men and women, to have captained in over 150 T20I games.
articles.body:
India’s long-serving captain of the women’s cricket team, Harmanpreet Kaur, has stepped down from the role across all formats, bringing down the curtain on a successful stint as she led the South Asian team to their first ICC Women’s World Cup title at home in 2025.

Kaur announced her decision in a social media post on Tuesday, two weeks after leading India to a successful defence of their gold medal at the Asian Games.

“Today, I step down as captain of the Indian Women’s Cricket Team across all formats,” she wrote in an Instagram post.

“This is not an easy decision. It carries years of memories, emotions, sacrifices, and moments that will stay with me for the rest of my life.”

The 37-year-old was the Twenty20 captain for more than a decade after assuming the role in 2016, followed by ODI and Test captaincy in 2022.

Kaur, who made her T20I and ODI debuts for India in 2009, has had an illustrious career as skipper.

Indian media reports said Kaur’s decision came a day after she met Devajit Saikia, secretary of the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI), ⁠to discuss the future of the women’s team.

Opening batter Smriti Mandhana, who has been Kaur’s deputy since 2022, is the favourite to take over the captain’s role.

Under Kaur’s captaincy, India won their maiden Women’s Cricket World Cup title in November last year on home soil.

Most recently, she led India to title defence at the Asian Games, thrashing Sri Lanka, just after lifting the Women’s Asia Cup trophy earlier in September.

The top-order batter helped India reach the semifinals of the 2018 and 2023 Women’s T20 World Cups, as well as finish runners-up in the 2020 edition.

Kaur has captained India in five Tests, 51 ODIs and 155 T20Is, and is also the first cricketer — male or female — to captain her side in international cricket in more than 150 T20I games.

“I leave the captaincy today with a heart full of emotions, but also with peace … because I genuinely believe my team is in a good place,” she said in her Instagram post. “I feel I have done my duty.

“Captaincy may end today, but my love for Indian cricket never will.

“Now, I’m ready to play for the love of the game again. Captaincy ends. The journey continues.”

articles.title: Sahibzada Farhan named Pakistan’s T20 captain as Naseem Shah returns
articles.summary: Salman Agha axed before T20 home series against Sri Lanka, but Shaheen Shah Afridi is retained as ODI captain.
articles.body:
Sahibzada Farhan has replaced Salman Ali Agha as Pakistan’s Twenty20 cricket captain, ushering in changes to the leadership and squad for the upcoming three-match home series against Sri Lanka.

Farhan led Pakistan to a silver-medal finish at the Asian Games, losing to India in the final on Sunday.

Batter Hasan Nawaz and fast bowler Naseem Shah were recalled to the T20 squad.

Nawaz had been out of favour since November, but in the Asian Games final he hit 96 and was out off the final ball as Pakistan lost by 19 runs.

Shah last played in the shortest format at the T20 World Cup in February. He was also added to the one-day international squad for the following tri-series with Sri Lanka and England.

Rising star Razaullah was rewarded for his impressive performance on his Test debut against England last month in Birmingham and was included in the T20 and ODI squads. He is yet to make his white-ball debut.

Fast bowler Shaheen Afridi was retained as ODI captain of a team that included Agha and Babar Azam.

But the selectors ignored Mohammad Rizwan because the wicketkeeper was under investigation by the National Cyber Crime Investigation Authority. Rizwan was one of the seven players who were summoned home after Pakistan lost the second Test to England at Lord’s in August.

Khawaja Nafay was the specialist wicketkeeper for the T20s while Ghazi Ghori, who made his Test debut in England, was the first-choice gloveman for the ODIs.

Rawalpindi will host the three Sri Lanka T20s from October 9-13. The tri-series begins on October 18.

Former Australian fast bowler Shaun Tait was named as Pakistan’s bowling coach after his recent stint with the Bangladesh team. Under Tait, Bangladesh beat Pakistan 2-0 in the Test series this year.

Tait replaced Ashley Noffke, who has been contracted by the Netherlands.

Pakistan T20 squad: Sahibzada Farhan (captain), Abdul Samad, Abrar Ahmed, Arafat Minhas, Fakhar Zaman, Hasan Nawaz, Muhammad Imran Randhawa, Khawaja Nafay, Maaz Sadaqat, Naseem Shah, Razaullah, Saim Ayub, Mohammad Salman Mirza, Shadab Khan, Sufiyan Moqim.

Pakistan ODI squad: Shaheen Shah Afridi (captain), Abrar Ahmed, Salman Ali Agha, Arafat Minhas, Babar Azam, Faheem Ashraf, Fakhar Zaman, Ghazi Ghori, Haris Rauf, Hasan Nawaz, Naseem Shah, Razaullah, Saad Baig, Saim Ayub, Shadab Khan, Sufiyan Moqim.

articles.title: From Tokyo to Nagoya: Lovlina Borgohain’s long road to the top of the podium | Exclusive Interview
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Lovlina Borgohain’s Asian Games gold was not just a medal upgrade from silver in the last edition.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Lovlina Borgohain’s Asian Games gold was not just a medal upgrade from silver in the last edition. It was the latest marker in a 15-year career that has taken the Assam boxer through Olympic success, injuries, difficult phases and a mentally demanding Paris 2024 campaign.At the 2026 Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Borgohain finally changed the colour of her Asian Games medal, defeating China’s Bao Ziyi 5-0 in the women’s 75kg final. The victory, on her 29th birthday, made her only the second Indian woman after MC Mary Kom to win boxing gold at the Asian Games -- 12 years after Kom’s 2014 triumph.For Borgohain, however, the gold's significance went beyond the history books.“It’s still difficult to get out of this moment. I still have the gold medal in my hand," said a beaming Borgohain while lifting the gold medal next to her face. "It’s a very special moment for me. I can’t express how I feel,” she continued as she spoke to TimesofIndia.com upon returning from Japan.Borgohain had finished with silver at the 2022 Hangzhou Asian Games, losing to China’s Li Qian in the final. Three years later, she returned to the continental stage determined to go one step further.I got a silver medal in the last Asian Games and this time I got a gold medal. This is why it is so special. And to do it on my birthday is extra specialHer path to the gold in Nagoya was not straightforward. She began with a 5-0 quarter-final win over South Korea’s Seong Su-yeon before edging Kazakhstan’s reigning 70kg world champion Natalya Bogdanova 3-2 in a closely fought semi-final. She then produced a 5-0 win over Ziyi in the final.The contrast with Hangzhou made the medal particularly meaningful.“Every event is very important. We believe that the Asian Games medal is the highest after the Olympics. I think this medal is shining amidst all the medals. The colour has changed. This medal means a lot to me,” Borgohain said.“I got a silver medal in the last Asian Games and this time I got a gold medal. This is why it is so special. And to do it on my birthday is extra special.”The victory also continued a curious connection between Borgohain and Japan. Five years ago, Tokyo had brought her an Olympic bronze medal — the breakthrough that changed the trajectory of her career.“I was very excited because I was going to Japan again. I had won a medal in (the) 2020 Olympics in Japan, and my life changed because of that,” she said.“I had a positive mindset before leaving India. I wanted to make it the best tournament of my life. I knew that I could do it because Japan is lucky for me.”My perspective has not changed because of the medal. When I lose, my self-belief remains the same. Sometimes I am confident, and sometimes I am down. But I am the same person that I was before‘Everything is a game of the mind’The gold also offered a reminder of Borgohain’s ability to rebuild.Her career has not followed a straight line since the Tokyo Olympics. Injuries, changes in form and the disappointment of the Paris Olympics tested her, while the pressure that came with becoming an Olympic medallist added another layer to the challenge.Borgohain does not, however, see the Asian Games gold as something that has fundamentally changed her.“I don’t think I am looking at myself differently because of this medal. I have won and lost a lot of medals. People’s perspective changes because of the medal. But I am always the same in my own eyes,” she said.“My perspective has not changed because of the medal. When I lose, my self-belief remains the same. Sometimes I am confident, and sometimes I am down. But I am the same person that I was before.”That mindset became particularly important after Paris 2024, when she failed to reach the medal rounds. Borgohain describes the period as one of the most difficult phases of her career.“I have a 15-year journey. Every time I go to a competition, my mindset is different. When we play, we reach the medal. It is not easy to recover from a tough period. The 2024 Paris Olympics wasn’t an easy period for me mentally,” she said.“But I think everything is a game of the mind. It depends on how we look at it. If we take tough things easy, it becomes easy. If we take easy things hard, it becomes hard. I think that helped me a lot to keep myself calm and relaxed.”It matters a lot for an athlete because of this medal I am qualifying for the World Championships. I am getting a good treat otherwise I would have to play the Nationals and follow the same processBorgohain qualifies for World ChampionshipsThe Asian Games victory has also given Borgohain a more direct route towards the next stage of her career. The gold means she qualifies for the World Championships, rather than having to go through the national selection route. A strong performance there could also put her on the road to another Olympic qualification campaign.“It matters a lot for an athlete because of this medal I am qualifying for the World Championships. I am getting a good treat otherwise I would have to play the Nationals and follow the same process,” she said.“So that is a big advantage of the medal, and it boosts my confidence that I can do better. If I do well there, then I can qualify for the Olympics also.”For now, though, Borgohain is resisting the temptation to look too far ahead.“There is a lot of planning. But not everything is the same. I am living in the present. I don’t know what will happen tomorrow. I will try to live like this. It makes me feel good. I will try to live like this.”‘Young athletes have stronger mindset’Borgohain’s gold was part of a strong boxing campaign for India at the Asian Games. India finished the competition with six boxing medals, including three golds, with Parveen Hooda and Ankush Panghal also winning their respective finals.In the Asian Games, our Indian team came out on top. I think our athletes are very strong. Their mentality is very good. We used to think that we would not be able to do it. But now our young athletes have the mindset that ‘we have to do itSome months back, Indian boxers had returned with 10 medals at the Glasgow Commonwealth Games, including seven golds. No country had won more golds in boxing at a single edition of the CWG. It was also India's largest haul in the sport in a CWG.For Borgohain, the improvement reflects a broader change in the mentality of Indian boxers.“We had a very good performance. Both men and women did very well. Everyone knows the results of the Commonwealth Games. The results of the Commonwealth Games changed the results of Indian Boxing,” she said.“In the Asian Games, our Indian team came out on top. I think our athletes are very strong. Their mentality is very good. We used to think that we would not be able to do it. But now our young athletes have the mindset that ‘we have to do it’.”She also pointed to the support structure around the team, including government backing and the environment created by the coaching staff led by Santiago Nieva.“The support of the government matters a lot. They don’t let us down. We are getting good competition. The environment of our foreign coaches, led by Santiago (Nieva), is very positive. That is why we are getting good results.”For Borgohain, then, the Asian Games gold is both an ending and a beginning — the end of a 12-year wait since Mary Kom’s historic gold and the completion of a personal journey from Hangzhou silver to Nagoya gold.But she is not treating it as a destination. The next target can wait. For now, she is content to live in the moment — with the gold medal still in her hand.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Dylan Larkin and the NHL Players Who Will Dominate the Trade Rumor Mill During the 2026-27 Season
articles.summary: On the eve of the 2026-27 NHL regular season, the Columbus Blue Jackets traded first-line winger Kirill Marchenko to the Toronto Maple Leafs for power forward Matthew Knies in a six-player deal.
articles.body:
On the eve of the 2026-27 NHL regular season, the Columbus Blue Jackets traded first-line winger Kirill Marchenko to the Toronto Maple Leafs for power forward Matthew Knies in a six-player deal .

Multi-player NHL trades of that magnitude are rare in today's salary-cap world, especially just before the regular season begins. It generated considerable buzz among fans and pundits, as well as anticipation of more significant activity in this season's trade market.

Marchenko and Knies regularly featured in our NHL Trade Boards during the offseason . They weren't the only notable players to surface as trade candidates; some of them will likely continue to feature in trade rumors this season.

Follow along as we look at five players we expect to dominate this season's NHL trade rumor mill from now until the March 1 trade deadline.

For the last four months, Winnipeg Jets goaltender Connor Hellebuyck has topped our NHL Trade Boards .

The three-time Vezina Trophy winner went public with his trade request in August, hoping to force a trade. He's currently suspended without pay by the Jets for not reporting to training camp last month.

After the Jets missed the playoffs last season, Hellebuyck criticized the club's overall performance, including his own. He hopes to win a Stanley Cup while still in his prime and believes a trade is the best path forward for himself and his family.

The 33-year-old goalie is signed through 2030-31 with an average annual value of $8.5 million. He has a full no-movement clause, but Chris Johnston of The Athletic reported that he's willing to waive it for a variety of teams.

The Jets were reportedly close to trading Hellebuyck to the Buffalo Sabres in June. However, the deal fell apart hours before the first round of the 2026 draft. He's also been linked to the Carolina Hurricanes, Utah Mammoth and San Jose Sharks.

Jets general manager Kevin Cheveldayoff has left the door open for Hellebuyck to return. Meanwhile, he's searching for a trade that makes sense for both sides.

Given the current standoff, it could take weeks or months until a deal takes place, ensuring Hellebuyck remains a fixture in the rumor mill.

Will he or won't he? That's the question plaguing the Minnesota Wild and their fans: Will Quinn Hughes sign an extension? He's in the final year of a six-year contract with a cap hit of $7.9 million.

The 26-year-old superstar defenseman is UFA-eligible next July. The uncertainty about his future earned him the No. 15 spot on our October NHL Trade Block Big Board .

It hasn't been because of a lack of effort by Wild general manager Bill Guerin. He made a big gamble by giving up three promising young players and a first-round pick to the Vancouver Canucks to acquire him last season, and he would love to get him signed for as long as possible.

Guerin had discussions with the Hughes camp throughout the offseason. However, he acknowledged that this was a big decision for the former Norris Trophy winner, and he didn't want to put too much pressure on him.

Plenty of time remains for both sides to get a deal done. Nevertheless, the longer Hughes goes unsigned, the more speculation there is about his future and the possibility of a trade by the March 1 deadline if he's still unsigned by then.

Since going public with his trade request in June, Detroit Red Wings center Dylan Larkin has regularly appeared in the rumor mill. For the past two months, he's sat at No. 2 on our NHL Trade Boards .

The 30-year-old is signed through 2030-31 with an average annual value of $8.7 million. He also carries a full no-movement clause.

Larkin initially identified the Minnesota Wild, Florida Panthers and Vegas Golden Knights as his preferred destinations. His list of acceptable destinations is reportedly broader, with Elliotte Friedman estimating roughly eight teams and naming the Colorado Avalanche, Washington Capitals, Dallas Stars and Tampa Bay Lightning as other possibilities.

Cap constraints and the Red Wings' asking price have complicated efforts to find a suitable deal. Detroit's ongoing search for a new general manager has also hampered efforts to move the two-way center.

As the season progresses, those factors could make it difficult for the Red Wings to trade Larkin. He might have to broaden his list of acceptable destinations or hope a strong performance persuades one of those teams to make an offer the Red Wings find compelling.

Jason Robertson's future with the Dallas Stars was a hot topic of speculation throughout last season and into the offseason.

Set to become a restricted free agent with arbitration rights, the 27-year-old was reportedly close to being traded to the Seattle Kraken in late June, but the proposed deal fell through after he declined their contract offer .

Robertson sat at No. 3 on our July NHL Trade Targets Ranking . He and the Stars eventually agreed to a one-year, $12 million contract, leaving the high-scoring winger eligible to become an unrestricted free agent next July.

During training camp, Stars general manager Jim Nill told The Athletic's Pierre LeBrun that he met with Robertson and his family this summer to mend their relationship . He stated that his priority is to open extension talks on Jan. 1, when they're eligible.

Things have been quiet since then, but Robertson could become a fixture in the rumor mill again if those discussions fail to yield a new contract before the March 1 trade deadline, especially if the Stars should struggle to maintain their place as a Stanley Cup contender.

First- and second-line centers are as scarce as hen's teeth in this season's NHL trade market. Between now and the March 1 trade deadline, teams that are seeking such players will maintain a close watch on pending unrestricted free agents who won't be re-signing with their clubs.

Pavel Zacha will draw the most attention. The Boston Bruins center is UFA-eligible next July, and he's the best option in a field of aging stars and bottom-six centers. He had a career-best 30 goals and 65 points last season and sits at No. 10 on our October NHL Trade Block Big Board .

On Oct. 1, TSN's Chris Johnston reported that Bruins management and the 29-year-old's camp have had ongoing contract discussions. However, finding the right salary number has been challenging because of skyrocketing salaries tied to the steep rise in the salary cap.

The Bruins will likely retain Zacha if they're pushing for a playoff berth this season. However, if they're struggling to stay in contention, they could entertain trade offers before the March trade deadline.

Contract and salary info via PuckPedia and CapWages.com .

articles.title: LA Knight's Do-or-Die Moment vs. Roman Reigns, New MITB Favorites, More WWE Raw Fallout
articles.summary: The October 5 episode of Raw on Netflix from the Enterprise Center in St. Louis, Missouri featured the final build to Money in the Bank 2026 in New Orleans, Louisiana.
articles.body:
The October 5 episode of Raw on Netflix from the Enterprise Center in St. Louis featured the final build to Saturday's Money in the Bank premium live event.

Roman Reigns appeared for the first time since Raw in Mexico City to face down LA Knight. Both men promised victory in their battle for the World Heavyweight Championship.

Stephanie Vaquer interfered in the No. 1 Contender's match between Becky Lynch and Liv Morgan, causing a no-contest and leading to a Women's World Championship Triple Threat announcement.

For all the fallout from Raw, including new favorites to win the men's and women's Money in the Bank ladder matches, keep reading.

LA Knight Should Win World Title at MITB vs. Roman Reigns

Calling for LA Knight to win the World Heavyweight Championship is a tired cause, but it is time to sell the idea once more.

The Megastar has remained significantly popular despite multiple rocky pushes that only led to midcard success.

He has shown that he can work at the level necessary to compete with Roman Reigns in PLE main events dating back to their first meeting at Crown Jewel in 2023.

If anyone would be an appropriate man to lose to Knight, it is WWE's top star and the man who cost him his first shot at the top.

Nearly three years past their first match, Knight may be looking at his last opportunity to be a world champion.

At 43 years old, he is competing with a rising number of stars under 30 who are looking for their first golden opportunity.

A loss to Reigns now would tell fans that Knight will never be good enough to compete at the level of The OTC, while others such as Oba Femi and Bron Breakker will win in this same scenario in the future.

Is it likely that The Megastar wins? No.

New Favorites Emerge to Win Money in the Bank

The two favorites to win this year's Money in the Bank ladder matches are Bron Breakker and Roxanne Perez, according to BetOnline .

Both make sense, though WWE has smartly set up several others to steal the victory instead.

For the women, Perez should be the favorite, especially since her win would cause drama within The Judgment Day, but Sol Ruca could be a dark horse given her strong booking on Raw.

Tiffany Stratton makes sense creatively due to the tension of her holding the Money in the Bank briefcase with her friend, Chelsea Green, as the champion, but it may be too soon for her to win a second time.

Lash Legend has been booked as dangerous, though it would be a mistake to push her to the world title scene this early.

Lola Vice and Jacy Jayne are intriguing future prospects, but neither is ready yet.

For the men, Bron Breakker, Penta and Kevin Owens all have compelling cases as fresh names who should be world champions within the next year.

Breakker fits the profile best as the fast opportunistic heel. KO has intriguing history to play on with a cash-in on Sami Zayn.

Penta would get the biggest cheer of anyone on a win, though WWE rarely gives the briefcase to a babyface, especially one who is unlikely to turn with a cash-in.

Trick Williams is a dark horse here, though he may not be quite ready to deliver in the ring at the level you need as WWE champion.

CM Punk will never need a Money in the Bank briefcase to be world champion, especially as a two-time winner. Je'Von Evans is likely just in the match for the high spots at this early stage of his career.

On both fronts, the field is intriguing, but the best bets look to be Breakker and Perez, who have proved their worth and are ready for the next step.

While tag team wrestling is still as relevant to professional wrestling as ever, WWE seems to be just about done with the concept.

The Vision have been world tag team champions for almost three months and have yet to defend the titles on television.

Instead, Bron Breakker is going after Money in the Bank while he and Austin Theory cannot even beat makeshift teams like Penta and Je'Von Evans.

While SmackDown is in a slightly better spot with The MFTs on top, the division is decidedly low card and separate from everything else going on.

The true exception is the women's tag team division, though even that has become less relevant to the product since WrestleMania 42.

Fatal Influence may be a dominant force on SmackDown, but any women's tag team outside of the blue brand has been forgotten in potential title contention.

Even when WWE threw together random main event stars to run the tag team division, it felt like the division mattered more than it does right now.

Solo Sikoa Ready for Huge Push to the Top

Solo Sikoa is back and as popular as he has ever been.

While questions remain of how he returned, he seems to be ready to work with The Usos to combat The 946.

That should be a temporary alliance as the best dynamic was Sikoa and LA Knight together, which can continue to elevate two popular underserved stars.

However, the time has come to test the waters again with Reigns.

Sikoa was once a top star on the rise, but the push went bad quickly. However, that angle required him to be a heel lacking personality.

He is finally showing his personality, and fans are ready to embrace him. The best answer is to run Sikoa up the card, perhaps all the way to the world title if fans keep supporting him.

Stop Booking the Same Lazy Triple Threat Setup

Since the return of Stephanie Vaquer and Becky Lynch, it has been clear that a Triple Threat for the Women's World Championship including Liv Morgan was inevitable.

Somehow WWE took so long to book it that the company had to hot-shot a last-minute non-finish for the go-home show of Money in the Bank to sell that match.

Booking a contender's match that ends in a non-finish to make both challengers contenders is lazy booking that was entirely avoidable.

Two weeks ago, La Primera announced she would fight both women for her title. A Triple Threat was the easy answer on that night.

Two weeks later, WWE got there by wasting weeks of television teasing two separate singles matches with no intention of delivering either at Money in the Bank.

This direction for Money in the Bank made Raw's top three women appear foolish and ended at the most predictable result with less buildup.

Sometimes, fewer complications can deliver greater rewards, and this was another case of WWE doing too much to deliver so much less.

articles.title: Washington officials won't budge on trans athlete policy after girl files SCOTUS appeal for alleged assault
articles.summary: WIAA and Washington's superintendent say transgender athletes can keep competing by gender identity as a Supreme Court application over wrestling pends.
articles.body: Washington’s high school athletics association and the state superintendent say they will keep letting students compete by gender identity while a Supreme Court application over girls’ wrestling is pending. The Washington Office of Superintendent of Public Instruction (OSPI) and Washington Interscholastic Activities Association (WIAA) responded after K.M.K. and her mother, Stephanie Lynne Brown, asked Justice Elena Kagan for an injunction pending appeal. The plaintiff is Kallie Keeler, the Puyallup-area wrestler who alleges she was sexually assaulted by a male opponent during a girls’ match in December and was not told he was male beforehand. OSPI, which does not run athletics but enforces state law on extracurricular activities, stood by current state policy. WASHINGTON FAMILY REQUESTS SCOTUS INJUNCTION AFTER DAUGHTER WAS ALLEGEDLY SEXUALLY ASSAULTED BY TRANS ATHLETE "While OSPI does not oversee athletics in our state, our office is responsible for communicating, upholding, and enforcing the law, including in student athletics and extracurricular activities," the superintendent’s office told OutKick. "OSPI will continue to uphold Washington’s current law unless or until the law changes. OSPI does not have any non-privileged statement, board notice, or guidance that we have issued to schools or staff regarding this appeal." After President Donald Trump signed an executive order in February 2025 aimed at keeping male athletes out of girls’ and women’s sports, Washington Superintendent Chris Reykdal rejected it outright. In a Feb. 6 statement, he said the order tried to force schools to "discriminate against trans female athletes" in exchange for federal funds, and that it sought to "restrict transgender girls from participating in girls’ sports with their peers." THE STATES THAT STILL ALLOW TRANS ATHLETES IN WOMEN'S SPORTS FACE QUESTIONS AFTER SUPREME COURT RULING He called the order unlawful, said it contradicted the Washington Law Against Discrimination and state school rules, and added: "Our state law prohibits discrimination on the basis of gender identity, and we will not back down from that." Days later, Reykdal went further on the categories themselves. "It is quite simply inaccurate to say, biologically, that there are only boys and there are only girls," he said. "There’s a continuum. There’s a science to this. There are children who are born intersex. There are children whose hormones and whose chromosomes are not consistent with their sex at birth." He told districts that students "get to identify and participate based on the gender in which they identify," and that his office would uphold that law. WHAT'S NEXT IN THE BATTLE TO 'SAVE WOMEN'S SPORTS' AFTER SCOTUS RULING — AND THE HIDDEN DAMAGE DRIVING IT He also framed the issue as a small accommodation. Of nearly a quarter million students in Washington interscholastic activities, he said, "roughly five to 10 youth have identified themselves as trans." "If we can’t accommodate the needs of five or 10 people," he asked, "who are we?" Reykdal argued an executive order is not law and does not override state policy. OSPI told districts to stay in compliance with the gender-identity rules and said it was preparing guidance in response to what it called an unlawful order. The WIAA also defended current state policy on Monday after Keeler's SCOTUS appeal. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! "The WIAA remains committed to following Washington State law which permits student-athletes to participate in sports consistent with the gender with which they identify," the association said. "If state law changes in the future, the WIAA holds the authority to revise policies as necessary to remain in compliance with state law. The WIAA will not comment further on a matter in litigation." Neither answer addressed the relief Keeler’s lawyers are seeking: that she be allowed to wrestle this season without being matched against a male, or that her mother receive notice so she can opt out without penalty. Wrestling in Washington opens in mid-November. Alliance Defending Freedom (ADF) filed the emergency application after a Tacoma federal judge denied a preliminary injunction on Aug. 23 and the Ninth Circuit refused an injunction pending appeal on Sept. 25. The filing argues that WIAA’s gender-identity rule violates Title IX and Brown’s parental rights. It cites the Supreme Court’s June 30 decision in West Virginia v. B.P.J., which held that states may limit girls’ teams to biological females. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Keeler has wrestled since she was 4. She left the team in January after the Lady Jag Kickoff and has said she is unsure she will return if she can be paired against a male again without warning. The district previously told her mother that forfeiture was the available remedy and that it would not give advance notice. The Puyallup School District did not respond to a request for comment.

articles.title: Raquel Avilés o cómo vencer el cáncer desde una piragua
articles.standfirst: La palista del equipo de dragonas BCS Sevilla, superviviente de esta enfermedad, compite en esta segunda edición de los Juegos del Agua de Melilla
articles.summary: La palista del equipo de dragonas BCS Sevilla, superviviente de esta enfermedad, compite en esta segunda edición de los Juegos del Agua de Melilla
articles.body: El Barco Dragón ha pasado de ser una disciplina minoritaria a convertirse en un auténtico aliado en la recuperación del cáncer, especialmente del de mama. El movimiento de paleo ayuda a prevenir el linfedema del brazo, una inflamación frecuente tras la extirpación de ganglios axilares o la radioterapia, y ofrece además un potente apoyo psicológico al crear un grupo de iguales que comparte vivencias y objetivos. Raquel Avilés, palista del equipo de dragonas BCS Sevilla, vicepresidenta del club y superviviente de cáncer, protagoniza una de las historias más inspiradoras de los II Juegos del Agua que se celebran en Melilla, organizados por ADESP y 11 Federaciones Deportivas Españolas. Esta semana, el programa de los Juegos acoge el Campeonato de España de Barco Dragón 1000M, organizado por la Federación Española de Piragüismo, una prueba en la que participarán 37 deportistas del BCS Sevilla, 17 de ellos mujeres supervivientes de cáncer. “Yo hacía diferentes tipos de deporte, he sido nadadora, y de adulta hacía gimnasio y poco más. Pero a raíz del cáncer vi que había un campeonato internacional de clubes en Sevilla en 2019 y decidí montar un equipo para representar a nuestra ciudad”, recuerda Raquel. En julio de ese año, el equipo debutó en el campeonato internacional y logró el subcampeonato en 2.000 metros, un resultado que supuso un revulsivo para seguir entrenando. El BCS Sevilla reúne a personas en diferentes momentos de la enfermedad: desde quienes acaban de salir del tratamiento hasta quienes conviven con un cáncer metastásico crónico. “No hay una pauta clara: si estás bien físicamente y puedes palear, puedes montarte en el barco”, explica. Los beneficios son tanto físicos como emocionales. “A nivel psicológico, el hecho de sentirte dentro de un grupo de iguales es muy potente. No es un grupo que viene a lamentarse, sino que utiliza el deporte como herramienta para entrar en una nueva etapa de la vida”. Algunas compañeras, añade, han podido dejar los antidepresivos tiempo después de conocer esta disciplina. En Melilla, el equipo compite mezclado en barcos mixtos, sin categoría específica para pacientes. “Nosotros primamos la inclusión. El ser paciente de cáncer ha sido una puerta para llegar al Barco Dragón, pero una vez dentro cada uno demuestra lo que vale. Siempre hemos querido quitarnos la etiqueta de enfermas: somos deportistas que han pasado por un cáncer”. Para Raquel, el mensaje es claro: “El cáncer paraliza y el Barco Dragón empuja”.

articles.title: Lewis Hamilton Posts Behind-the-Scenes Video of Restoration of Ultra Rare Ferrari F40
articles.summary: One month after showing up in Italy in his Ferrari F40 prior to the Italian Grand Prix, Lewis Hamilton has offered a more in-depth look at the iconic car.
articles.body:
One month after showing up in Italy in his Ferrari F40 prior to the Italian Grand Prix, Lewis Hamilton has offered a more in-depth look at the iconic car.

In a video posted on his YouTube channel, Hamilton walks viewers through the months-long process of restoring the Ferrari F40.

In an Instagram post on Aug. 31, Hamilton wrote he got his "very own F40" and it was the "car of my dreams" that he had been wanting since he was a kid:

"These cars are works of art and incredibly rare, so when I found this one, covered in dust after being sat in a garage for over thirty years, I knew I had to bring her home. First to Maranello, where the master engineers and mechanics at the factory worked for weeks to bring her back to life. Massive thank you to everyone who had a hand in this project. This has truly been a dream come true. I can't wait to share more with you all. "

Per ESPN's Laurence Edmondson , the Ferrari F40 was in production from 1987 to '92. There were only around 1,315 made during that period. It was also the last model to receive personal approval from Enzo Ferrari prior to his death in 1988.

Given how few of the cars were produced, their values typically range between $2.5-4 million , with the highest sale price on record being $11.5 million at a Sotheby's auction in August 2025.

Hamilton first showed off the luxury sports car in Monza as he prepared for the Italian Grand Prix.

Hamilton joined the Ferrari team for the 2025 F1 season. He finished sixth overall in his first year with the club, but he has taken steps forward so far in 2026.

The 41-year-old is currently third in the standings and won the Barcelona-Catalunya Grand Prix in June, his first victory since the 2024 season.

articles.title: 5 Landing Spots for Simon Edvinsson After Reported Trade Request from Red Wings
articles.summary: The Detroit Red Wings' offseason of drama has taken another turn as the team struggles to get restricted free agent defenseman Simon Edvinsson to re-sign.
articles.body:
The Detroit Red Wings' offseason of drama has taken another turn as the team struggles to get restricted free agent defenseman Simon Edvinsson to re-sign.

Edvinsson is one of two unsigned restricted free agents in the NHL (joining Carolina Hurricanes defenseman Alexander Nikishin), and word surfaced on Saturday that he might prefer a trade over re-signing with the Red Wings .

The whole situation just adds to the messiness of the Red Wings offseason, which has also included a trade request from center Dylan Larkin, his being stripped of his captaincy, the team not having a full-time general manager, and an inability to re-sign Edvinsson.

What makes the Edvinsson situation so much more frustrating is that they have the salary cap space to sign him, while he clearly wanted to be there after showing up at training camp, even without a new deal.

Now he is in Sweden with no deal, and according to Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman on Saturday, he would prefer a trade away from the Red Wings rather than signing a long-term deal.

Will a team come forward with an offer sheet? At this point, the Red Wings might actually prefer that because they could easily match it and end this headache.

But let's go with the idea that they will at least consider his trade request and try to identify some teams that could be a potential landing spot for his services.

What Would a Simon Edvinsson Trade Look Like?

An easy comparison here is the New Jersey Devils' trade of defenseman Šimon Nemec to the Calgary Flames earlier this offseason, which ultimately cost the Flames two future first-round picks.

From a box score perspective, the two players are somewhat comparable in their production.

Nemec has scored 16 goals and tallied 49 points in 155 career games, while Edvinsson has scored 19 goals and tallied 60 points in 175 career games.

Edvinsson is probably the better all-around player and played a bigger role with the Red Wings this past season as part of a top-pairing alongside Moritz Seider. When Edvinsson and Seider were on the ice together during 5-on-5 play in the 2025-26 season, the Red Wings outscored opponents 51-38 and had a 55 percent expected goals share.

When neither player was on the ice, those numbers dropped to a 66-95 deficit and a 45.7 percent expected goals share.

If there is a red flag here for Edvinsson, it's that his numbers away from Seider also took a big hit. Is his strong play the result of being paired with a Norris-caliber defenseman? Or is he capable of carrying a defensive pairing and being a top-pairing player on his own merits?

But that was (and still is) the wild card with Nemec, and New Jersey still managed to get multiple first-round picks for him while he signed a $7.25 million-per-season contract .

Something like that, or a comparable player value, should be the starting point for the Red Wings.

So let's take a look at a few teams that could (or should) be interested.

Trading Edvinsson within the division would be a nightmare PR move for a franchise already dealing with its share of them, but the Bruins are definitely a team that would need a player like Edvinsson.

Even though the Bruins were a playoff team a year ago, there was not much to like about their overall defensive structure. And there has not been much to like about it for the past few years.

In 2025-26 alone, the Bruins allowed 2.93 expected goals per 60 minutes of 5-on-5 play, the third-worst mark in the NHL, ahead of only the Vancouver Canucks and Chicago Blackhawks. That is not the type of company you want to be keeping. It was not much better in 2024-25.

The only reason the Bruins were able to contend and make the playoffs a year ago was that starting goalie Jeremy Swayman put together an elite year and carried the team on his back.

A No. 1 center has been a big priority for the Bruins. But another top-pairing defenseman would also be a nice addition, especially if it is someone who could pair well with right-handed Charlie McAvoy.

Boston has four first-round picks over the next three years, including two in the 2027 NHL Draft class.

Even though it has not been a full-scale, tear-everything-down, rebuild, the Pittsburgh Penguins are still going through a rebuild of sorts and keeping their eye on the future. General manager Kyle Dubas has repeatedly said they will be in the market for any young player who becomes available, and they have been very aggressive in exploring that market. It has worked out well at times.

Edvinsson would seem to be a natural fit.

Not only because he is still only 23 years old and fits the mold of the type of player they are interested in, but also because he would fill a major long-term position of need.

At the start of the 2026-27 season, the left side of the Penguins' defense (which is the side Edvinsson plays) consists of Sam Girard, Declan Carlile, and Trevor van Riemsdyk.

Girard is an unrestricted free agent after this season, while van Riemsdyk is 35 years old, and Carlile is still a bit of an unknown as to how good he can be long-term.

Especially when you look at the right side of the defense, where Erik Karlsson is an unrestricted free agent after this season (and 36 years old), and Kris Letang is 39.

They could really use a potential top-pairing defenseman who will be there for the next seven-plus seasons.

They have all of their future draft picks, including seven second-round picks over the next three years. They also have an exceptionally deep group of NHL-level forwards and some prospects that could be dangled as trade bait. One such prospect: Forward Will Horcoff, who is also the son of Red Wings interim general manager Shawn Horcoff.

If they are not already calling, they should be.

Players That Will Dominate the Rumor Mill

Seattle needs more impact players, or potential impact players.

It tried to take a big swing for Jason Robertson in the offseason, going so far as to have the trade agreed to and a $15 million-per-year contract offer, only for Robertson not to want to re-sign there.

They should keep taking swings, and Edvinsson would be a big long-term need.

Along with an underwhelming defense on paper, Seattle's best left-shot defenseman is Vince Dunn, who is also a potential unrestricted free agent after this season, leaving his future very much in doubt.

If Dunn leaves, you're going to need another top-pairing left-shot defenseman.

If you can get Dunn re-signed, you now have a Dunn-Edvinsson duo on the left side of your defense that should be a solid 1-2 punch.

Keep taking swings until you land somebody.

The Blues have been overhauling a lot of their roster and trying to turn over their core with younger, on-the-rise players.

Robert Thomas is one of the most underrated players in the NHL and is an elite playmaker at center.

Jake Neighbours, Jimmy Snuggerud, Mason McTavish and Dylan Holloway is an intriguing group of forwards that are just entering their prime years. Connor McMichael, after coming over in the Jordan Kyrou trade this offseason, is also on that list.

Philip Broberg has turned into an outstanding player at the top of their blue line.

It remains to be seen just how good this group can be, but it's an interesting team with some good players.

There are, however, still many holes, and the defense is one of them.

They have Broberg and Cam Fowler on the left side of their defense, but Fowler is 34 and probably not a great long-term option as a top-four defenseman. He's been solid in St. Louis, but they can do better in the top four.

The Blues have been linked to Carolina Hurricanes defenseman Alexander Nikishin, who is in the same situation as Edvinsson, so it is reasonable to conclude that they might also be interested in Edvinsson (unless they simply like Nikishin more as a player). The Blues still have all of their first-round draft picks in the coming seasons.

Another team in the division could be a PR headache for the Red Wings, but it's a divisional team with a big need and might be willing to pay up, even if a "divisional tax" is in play.

Even after adding Darren Raddysh over the summer, the Maple Leafs' defensive overhaul should not be finished, and Edvinsson would be a good fit for what they need.

Toronto has dealt many young players, prospects, and draft picks over the years, and most recently traded away perhaps its best trade chip, forward Matthew Knies.

Would somebody like Easton Cowen be of interest to the Red Wings as a potential focal point? He is still only 21 years old and had a strong rookie season, and even though dealing Edvinsson would leave a big hole in the Red Wings' defense that would need to be filled, the forward depth needs to be filled out as well.

articles.title: Flyers on Wrong Side of NHL History With Rare Stat Amid Winless Start to 2026 Season
articles.summary: The Philadelphia Flyers are off to one of the most lopsided winless season starts in NHL history.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Flyers are off to one of the most lopsided winless season starts in NHL history.

The Flyers have been outscored 17-5 and outshot 158-76 during the team's 0-2-2 start to the 2026-27 campaign.

That marks the second-largest shot deficit through four NHL games for any team since 1959, according to Flyers reporter Wayne Fish.

Players That Will Dominate the Rumor Mill

The Flyers have gone 0-for-11 on the power play in their first four games while getting badly outshot from the slot and off the rush, per NHL Network's Mike Kelly.

The Flyers were coming into the campaign off a strong finish to last season, during which they went 6-2-0 in April to secure a playoff spot for the first time since 2020 before eliminating the Pittsburgh Penguins from the first round.

Rick Tocchet's team has yet to build on that campaign. The Flyers opened this season with a 7-0 loss to the Penguins, then blew consecutive third-period leads in overtime losses to the New Jersey Devils and Carolina Hurricanes.

"You have to get the puck. You have to execute plays," Tocchet said about getting outshot 40-18 in the loss to the Hurricanes. "Our execution is not good this year. It really isn't. And if you don't execute, you're not going to get shots."

The Flyers were most recently outshot 36-14 in a 4-1 Monday night loss to the Tampa Bay Lightning during which Tocchet said his team was "way too comfortable."

Philadelphia general manager Danny Briere attempted to add a top-line center by offer sheeting Leo Carlsson this offseason, only to see the deal matched by the Anaheim Ducks.

That left the Flyers for the most part running things back with the relatively inexperienced roster that took this franchise back to the playoffs last season.

The Fourth Period's David Pagnotta reported ahead of the season start the Flyers were "believed to be eyeing defensive depth" after adding only Simon Benoit to the blue line this offseason.

At least one offseason addition has already been making an impact for the Flyers. Goaltender Joseph Woll, who was acquired alongside Benoit from the Toronto Maple Leafs in June, kept the Flyers competitive in both their overtime losses despite his team's lack of offensive production.

Briere could hope adding defensive depth will help the Flyers support Woll and Dan Vladar as Tocchet's young offense works on gelling down the stretch, starting with a Thursday evening road game against the Ottawa Senators.

articles.title: Paying attention to the Arizona Fall League
articles.summary: Is anyone any good in Arizona for the Phillies?
articles.body:
I am no scout, though I'm pretty sure by this point I can tell the difference between a good baseball player and a bad baseball player. Projecting which players will be good, though, simply by watching workouts and game action and coming away with knowing what I'm talking about is still a science I don't full grasp. It's every season where I hear about something that still makes me appreciate those that can do it and do it with pretty good accuracy.

Rarely have I watched the Arizona Fall League at any point in a season, mostly because my baseball focus was solely on the Phillies and how they were faring in the playoffs. That has of course changed with the Phillies currently at home for the offseason and some of their better prospects getting some run down Arizona. It's because of those prospects that more attention should be given to those games as they are going to have some say in how the Phillies approach their offseason plans. Maybe they aren't going to chart the ultimate course of action the team decides to take, but several of the players that are there will have some bearing on what the Phillies plan to do.

The highest profile name the Phillies have sent there, Miller's performance is likely going to play a part in several decisions the team makes. As you already know, Miller did miss most of the 2026 season with a back injury that needed some kind of procedure done, but he returned healthy enough to get a week's worth of games in at the end of the regular season before helping Reading win the Eastern League championship. When he did return, there was rust on his frame, but there were glimpses!

How he performs in Arizona will probably not determine if he makes the major leagues out of spring training or not, but it will likely influence the roster on the fringes. He's on a team that also includes Sebastian Walcott on the roster, arguably the top hitting prospect in the game today, so getting Miller every day at bats in Arizona will be a challenge. Let's say he shows that he's still one of the better hitting prospects in the game in these few weeks. Does the team decided to prop open the door for him to win a spot in Clearwater? Do they move Trea Turner in deference to his impending arrival? Do they sign someone as a stopgap in order to not block him at shortstop? Is shortstop even his final home or is a move to third base already in the cards? He's played only one game so far and that came at third to make room for another shortstop there, Welbyn Francisca from the Guardians system.

Of course, the entire thing will depend on how Miller ultimately holds up healthwise. The team is likely just hoping he has a good, solid six weeks of health and plate appearances to make up for some of the time he lost this year. It wouldn't surprise anyone if he was held back a bit by the team to make sure there is nothing going wrong. You can imagine that the slightest tweak of anything and he is going home for the winter.

Realistically, it would be unfair to place too much stock in how he performs and let that influence the team's decision making. He just needs to get the work in, not worry about how it'll set his place for 2027. He's going to make his debut next year at some point. It'll just depend on next year more than anything he does in Arizona. Still, he's easily the most interesting watch they have.

Escobar was arguably the team's best hitting prospect besides Miller coming into 2026 and he flat stunk the joint up. Pretty much everything that he was good at took a step backwards this year, lowering his stock within the organization quite a bit. There was a time when his name would come in trade discussions about how he was the best prospect the team could move at the deadline while getting something real back in return. Now, that idea seems too foreign to actually occur.

The team will need to make a decision on whether or not to place him on the 40 man roster this offseason, a decision that was pretty easy prior to this year. It still is thanks to the dearth of hitting prospects this team has, but if he isn't going to take some steps back in the right direction, the team may want to think twice before taking the plunge on the roster spot. He needs to have a good showing in Arizona to show that he is worthy of a roster and/or worth another team taking a shot on him in a deal this offseason.

Neither Nori nor Hettiger would be something teams would classify as a "top prospect". Pay no mind to the fact that Nori is a first round draft pick. He wasn't considered one then by people on the outside and really hasn't done anything to sway that opinion since.

Yet within the Phillies farm system, he is still seen as someone who might potentially fit a role with the team. That speaks more to their lack of actual hitting prospects than anything else, but finding competent role players from within the organization is one of the biggest reasons the Phillies have started to show more cracks in the armor at the major league level. Nori's performance in Arizona won't go very far in determining if he can earn a starting position as that's not really on the table. His ever being penciled into a big league lineup with regularity is likely off the table. But consider that Felix Reyes was batting cleanup at one point this year. Gabriel Rincones was given lots of chances to see what he could do. Heck, even Otto Kemp was touted as an option in the outfield for the team. The chances are there for minor league players to earn playing time in this outfield. Nori needs to start putting things together if he wants to be among the many that are given that chance.

The very same could be said about Hettiger. The team has very few catching prospect in their farm system and willingly gave playing time to Garrett Stubbs and Rafael Marchan. They are begging for players within the organization to take a step forward to claim a backup role on the team. There might even be some chances to start games!

Stubbs was on a playoff roster…on purpose!

Opportunities abound if only players take it and seize it. Hettiger finished the year in Reading, making it unlikely that he's going to reach Philadelphia any time soon. Yet good performances can sometimes springboard a player into having a good season the following year. Perhaps he can gain a better standing with the team by showing that there is still a good prospect in there, somewhere.

The Arizona Fall League isn't the greatest baseball being played. Pitchers don't pitch long, players leave at the slightest sign of injury and generally, it's played during the MLB playoffs, meaning our focus is elsewhere. Yet the Phillies have some interesting guys at play this year. How they do can help answer some questions about this team's future.

articles.title: 2026 Minor League Season Review: St. Lucie Mets
articles.summary: Reviewing the 2026 St. Lucie Mets season.
articles.body:
First Half Record: 33-33 (2/4 Florida State League East)

Second Half Record: 25-39 (3/4 Florida State League East)

The 2025 St. Lucie Mets were a powerhouse. The team went 34-31 in the first half to win the Florida State League East Division and went 43-22 in the second half, once again finding themselves atop the standings. They met the Daytona Tortugas in the FSL East Divisional Series but fell two games to one, ending their season.

The 2026 team, on the other hand, at no point were really that relevant of a team. In the first half, they went an even 33-33 to end the season second in the division, but they still found themselves 4.0 games behind the first place Jupiter Hammerheads. In the second half, they were a dismal 25-39, somehow not last in the division but irrelevant in the standings all the same.

Towards the end of the season, some of the 2026 draftees began making appearances, but outside of individual milestones or appearances, the 2026 St. Lucie Mets season wasn't particularly fun or exciting.

Elian Peña: 96 G, 365 AB, .271/.388/.397, 99 H, 18 2B, 2 3B, 8 HR, 61 BB, 94 K, 28/37 SB, .343 BABIP

Considered one of the best players available in the 2025-2026 international free agent class, and potentially the best position player available, the Mets and Elian Peña agreed to a $5 million dollar signing bonus, shattering the prior organizational record (Yovanny Rodriguez, $2.85 million) and eating up the majority of the $6,261,600 that the team had in their 2025-2026 pool.

Assigned to the Dominican Summer League, the 17-year-old Peña has had an interesting start to his career. It took him nearly two weeks to log his first professional hit, going 0-fer from June 2nd until June 14th. After finally getting over that hurtle, Peña hit an incredible .351/.467/.635 over the course of the rest of the season, hitting .292/.421/.528 in total with 13 doubles, 1 triple, 9 home runs, 21 stolen bases in 25 attempts, and 36 walks to 36 strikeouts in 55 games.

He was promoted to the Low-A St. Lucie Mets for the 2026 season and a somewhat divisive year. In total, he appeared in 96 games for St. Lucie and hit .271/.388/.397 with 18 doubles, 2 triples, 8 home runs, 28 stolen bases in 37 attempts, and 61 walks to 94 strikeouts. For large stretches of the season, Elian Peña looked meek at the plate, going up and alternating between taking too many pitches or taking bad hacks. For other stretches, he looked like a star, spraying the ball around the field and pulling fly balls for homers. Regardless of the actual offensive value he created, Peña spent the year playing against pitchers and fielders three years older than him, on average, and that in and of itself is a major positive. In late August, he was promoted to High-A Brooklyn and appeared in 15 games for them, hitting .164/.250/.224 in a ballpark that is the exact antithesis of his left-handed pull-and-lift approach.

Emilio Obispo: 14 G (10 GS), 53.1 IP, 43 H, 19 R, 12 ER (2.03 ERA), 24 BB, 54 K, .285 BABIP

Emilio Obispo was signed by the Mets in May 2024, just prior to the start of the 2024 Dominican Summer League season. The Dominican right-hander was given a low five-figure signing bonus and was suiting up for the DSL Mets a few weeks later. The 17-year-old right-hander appeared in 9 games for the DSL Mets Orange, starting all of them, and posted a 3.47 ERA in 36.1 innings, allowing 21 hits, walking 12, and striking out 41. He was assigned to the FCL Mets for the 2025 season but never actually played, missing the entire season due to an injury.

Obispo returned to the mound in 2026, and after analyzing his progress during extended spring training, the Mets made the decision to begin the season in Low-A St. Lucie, a challenging assignment for the 19-year-old. He rewarded the faith that scouts and evaluators in the organization had in him by posting a 2.03 ERA in 53.1 innings over 10 starts and 4 relief appearances, allowing 43 hits, walking 24, and striking out 54. In late July, the right-hander was promoted to High-A Brooklyn, where he appeared in 6 games with them, all starts, and posted a 3.76 ERA in 27.0 innings, allowing 23 hits, walking 12, and striking out 28.

Obispo throws from a low-three-quarters arm slot with a long arm action through the back. He does not push off or extend much off the mound and as such, his whippy arm has a comparatively high release point. The right-hander throws a sinker, four-seam fastball, changeup, and curveball. During his time with St. Lucie, he threw his sinker roughly 45% of the time, his changeup 25% of the time, his curveball 20% of the time, his four-seam fastball 10% of the time.

Obispo's sinker sits in the high-80s-to-high-90s, the volatility in its velocity highlighting the potential but unpredictability in 19-year-old right-hander. Averaging 93 MPH, the pitch features 18 inches of horizontal arm-side break, above-average for a sinker. Florida State League batters hit .217/.330/.265 against it with a 22% whiff rate. His four-seam fastball finds itself in roughly the same velocity range, sitting in the low-to-high-90s, averaging 94 MPH, but because it does not feature much backspin or sidespin, it features fringe-average life and below-average induced vertical break, resulting in batters hitting a healthy .273/.333/.500 against it with a suboptimal 8% whiff rate.

His changeup sits in the low-to-high-80s, averaging 84 MPH. With a spin rate ranging between 1,500 and 2,150, the pitch has averaged an average 35 inches of vertical drop and an above-average 18 inches of horizontal arm-side fade. The pitch has been Obispo's best offering, limited FSL batters to a .169/.247/.292 slash line with an impressive 46% whiff rate.

His curveball sits in the mid-70s-to-low-80s, averaging 80 MPH. The pitch has a low spin rate, averaging 2220 RPM, resulting in a big, loopy pitch that doesn't have much bite. Obispo occasionally struggles to land it in the strike zone, and batters hit .276/.364/.310 against it with a 36% whiff rate. Occasionally, he will fire one off that has sharper bite, and has the appearance of a gyro slider rather than a curveball.

articles.title: TNIAAM WBB roundtable: our thoughts on the 2026-27 schedule
articles.summary: Interesting slate ahead for WBB this season.
articles.body:
The Syracuse Orange women's basketball team is just weeks away from beginning a new season, and it's time to start looking at what's ahead in 2026-27.

Dom and Audrey share their thoughts and early predictions for the Orange with the full WBB schedule now out.

Overall thoughts on the 2026-27 schedule?

Dom: The first five games of the season should allow this mostly new team to gel and build chemistry. In both the non-conference and ACC slate, the middle portions ramp up very fast, so the Orange will need to get off to hot starts in both, survive the middle, and then surge at the end.

Audrey: I feel cautiously optimistic. My biggest worry is the tough ACC slate in late December/early January, but there are a lot of opportunities before and after that stretch to farm some wins for both cushion and momentum.

How are you feeling about the non-con slate?

Dom: To have high hopes of making the tournament, Syracuse must go at least 2-1 against the following opponents it will see in a row: Wisconsin and Auburn in Puerto Rico, then Oklahoma on the road for the ACC/SEC Challenge. Neither Wisconsin nor Auburn are in ESPN's latest bracketology; Oklahoma is a six seed. Picking up two non-con wins against other P4 schools will do wonders for the resume, but dropping either Wisconsin or Auburn without a dub over Oklahoma could be a blemish that could bite later in the spring.

Audrey: Oklahoma scares me, Auburn will be an adequate opponent, and the rest of the non-conference teams the Orange will face do not strike fear into my heart. I imagine that, should the Orange fall to squads from Southern, Le Moyne, or Bucknell, it will be that the Orange defeated themselves, more than anything their opponents did.

Toughest stretch in the ACC schedule for Syracuse?

Dom: After SMU followed by the last two non-con games, Syracuse gets Duke, North Carolina, and Virginia Tech in consecutive games. All of those are tournament-caliber teams, and it's such a big ramp-up compared to facing Le Moyne and Bucknell. Of note, that stretch starts after a 10-day gap between Duke and the last non-con game.

Audrey: It has to be the Duke/North Carolina/Virginia Tech stretch or the NC State /Louisville/Virginia stretch. Most of those teams are regularly towards the top of not only the ACC, but the entire Division I standings. Of the aforementioned groups, Syracuse only has a positive historical record against Virginia. All of these teams are equipped to give the Orange a very tough challenge.

Most important stretch in the ACC schedule for Syracuse?

Dom: The entire month of January. Outside Notre Dame, the other seven ACC games this month are against non-tournament projected programs. Going 7-1 with the lone loss being to Notre Dame likely cements a trip to the Big Dance for the Orange if it can perform well in the non-con.

Audrey: January is full of trap games. I think Syracuse will have a better record than, say, Stanford, Cal, and Florida State on each respective game day, but the relative lack of experience on this Orange team may make some of these matchups closer than they ought to be. If 'Cuse can stay focused and avoid playing down to the level of their competition, I think this is a sneaky opportunity to rack up conference wins heading into the postseason.

Dom: If the Notre Dame game was later in the schedule, that would be the easy contender. NC State in February is the next-best pick; think this is a worse Wolfpack squad than fans are used to.

Audrey: Picture this: it's New Year's Eve, three feet of snow surrounds the JMA Wireless Dome, and for the first time since last season, Sophie Burrows' name rings on the PA speakers . . . for North Carolina. I understand that tuning into the Syracuse WBB game may not be on the NYE agenda for many, but I think this game will show what this team is made of, for better or for worse. North Carolina is routinely a challenge for the Orange, SU coming up short in their past three matchups, and facing Burrows and company head-on in the Dome can absolutely swing the momentum into the New Year for the Orange.

Early prediction time: what is the floor and ceiling for this year's team?

Dom: At bare minimum, this is a team that will at least be on the bubble. Izoje is that good to will the Orange to a few more games than expected. I don't think this is a top-four team in the conference, but it can definitely get to the five-to-eight seed range.

Audrey: This Orange team is big, literally. More than half of the roster exceeds a six-foot frame, with Uche Izoje leading the charge. Coach Jack is excellent at maximizing players, so I expect to see the Orange shine especially on the defensive end of the floor. I anticipate a big leap from Izoje and lots of energy from all the new faces 'Cuse brought in. Like Dom said, I don't think this group is past the likes of Duke, Louisville or UNC, but I think they can hang with Notre Dame and NC State in the upper-middle echelon of the ACC and even advance a round or two in the NCAA Tournament.

Now it's your turn: how are you feeling about the Orange's 2026-27 schedule? Which women's basketball games are you looking forward to most this season?
