articles.title: Has LSU already put the Ole Miss loss behind them?
articles.summary: The Tigers have responded with back-to-back dominant wins. Have they officially moved past their first loss?
articles.body:
There's no question that LSU's first loss of the Lane Kiffin era carried some weight.

When the Tigers fell 32-24 to Ole Miss and dropped their record to 2-1, there were plenty of questions about how they would respond. Two weeks later, it is becoming easier to believe LSU has put that loss behind them.

The Tigers have responded with back-to-back dominant victories, first beating No. 23 Texas A&M 35-6 before dismantling McNeese 63-14. LSU has now scored 98 points across its last two games while allowing just 20.

The Texas A&M game is the more important part of the equation.

LSU did not simply beat the Aggies. They dominated a ranked SEC opponent on both sides of the football.

Obviously, LSU was expected to win the game comfortably, but the Tigers did exactly what they were supposed to do. They scored 63 points, gained 731 yards and set a school record with 101 offensive plays.

That does not erase what happened against Ole Miss and what still needs to be cleaned up.

Although it does make the loss feel less concerning than it did two weeks ago.

LSU is now 4-1 and has another SEC game coming up at Kentucky. The Tigers have already shown they can respond to adversity, and that could become one of the more important traits of this team as the schedule gets tougher.

The real test is whether LSU can carry this momentum into conference play.

For now, though, it is fair to wonder if the Ole Miss loss was simply a bad night rather than a sign of what this team will ultimately become under Kiffin.

articles.title: Positive and concerning signs coming out of Packers' win over Buccaneers
articles.summary: The Packers' win over the Bucs featured both positive and concerning signs for Matt LaFleur's team.
articles.body:
In beating the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday, the Green Bay Packers won a regular season football game in regulation for the first time since last December. In a must-win game, the Packers accomplished the mission.

But beating a winless team by only three points means the performance was far from perfect, and the visitors certainly did not play a clean game in Tampa.

Breaking down the positive and concerning signs coming out of Sunday's win over the Bucs:

Jordan Love was under pressure on only four of his 31 dropbacks, per PFF. That's an incredible improvement over the first three weeks, when he had individual drives where he was under pressure on at least four dropbacks. Love said he was more comfortable in the pocket, and the tape backs his words.

Love was kept mostly clean in the pocket, and he produced his best game of the season passing. Amazing how that works. He completed 22 of 30 passes, and four of the eight incompletions were clear drops. Love threw a late interception, but that play was less a poor one from the quarterback and more an incredible play by the defensive back. Protect Love and good things happen.

Matt LaFleur called play-action more in this game, and Love was excellent off run fakes, completing 8-of-9 passes for 79 yards and a touchdown. A lot of it was off boot action. The Packers also got an explosive play out of 13 personnel to Mark Redman -- the team's blocking tight end -- off a run fake. A mix of quick game and play-action could be the fix for the Packers passing game.

The run game hit two explosive plays, both setting up scores. It's a start. Taking out the kneeldowns to end the game, the Packers had 98 rushing yards. Again, it's a glimmer of hope for a run game that needs to come alive.

The rookie kicker hit a 58-yarder before the half, eventually providing the difference between the two teams. Trey Smack is becoming a reliable weapon. His only miss through four games was blocked, and he's 2-for-2 on kicks over 55 yards. Nice to have a kicker who can extend your scoring range out to 60 yards or more.

The run defense bounced back. Bucky Irving didn't have a run over seven yards, and the Bucs finished with only 76 total rushing yards on designed runs to running backs. Jalon Daniels burned them on a few scrambles, but the run defense was able to contain Irving and put the game mostly in the rookie quarterback's hands.

The drops are out of control. Bo Melton dropped a pass that would have converted a third down, created an explosive play and put the Packers into the red zone. Tucker Kraft dropped a touchdown pass. Matthew Golden had a third-down conversion knocked out of his hands. Skyy Moore dropped a quick screen. This has become a recurring problem to start 2026. The Packers have dropped 12 of Love's passes, the most in the NFL through four weeks.

How much of the improvement along the offensive line was actually real? Jordan Love got the ball out of his hands on average of 2.20 seconds, by far the fastest among quarterbacks in Week 4, and 22 of his 31 dropbacks saw him get rid of the ball in under 2.5 seconds. The offensive line got a ton of help in this game. In the true dropback passing game, the Packers allowed pressure on four of 13 dropbacks, and four of the five offensive linemen gave up at least one pressure in true pass sets, per PFF. It wasn't perfect, and it's fair to wonder if the Packers can live in quick game all the time and still function consistently.

The defense finished off the game, but what could have been a convincing 24-14 or 31-14 win ended up being a nail-biter because the offense couldn't convert two golden scoring chances into points. Finish! Against just about any other opponent, the Packers would have been in big danger of blowing this game. Facing an undrafted rookie quarterback helped bail out the offense after two big mistakes late.

The offense committed eight penalties, continuing another concerning trend. The offensive line was responsible for five of the penalties, and the Packers had three false starts. Five of the penalties came on 1st-and-10. This Packers offense isn't good enough to be consistently facing 1st-and-15 or 1st-and-20.

The run game produced 86 yards. But if you take away the 58 yards on the two explosive runs, the other 17 designed runs to running backs gained all of 27 yards, or 1.6 yards per carry. So the run game still has a long way to go. Including plays negated by penalty, the Packers had nine runs gaining less than a yard. There was a lot of empty plays in the run game.

articles.title: Lakers’ skinny Luka Doncic the butt of a JJ Redick joke after effortless domination of Kings
articles.summary: Luka Doncic has clearly taken his Los Angeles Lakers stint seriously, and the Lakers superstar’s noticeably skinny appearance is strong evidence of that comm...
articles.body:
Luka Doncic has clearly taken his Los Angeles Lakers stint seriously, and the Lakers superstar's noticeably skinny appearance is strong evidence of that commitment. The slimmer-looking Luka helped lead the Lakers to a 127-103 victory over the Sacramento Kings in their first preseason game, and head coach JJ Redick is much impressed.

Following Doncic's stellar preseason performance, Redick explained that the Lakers superstar put considerable effort into improving his conditioning throughout the summer.

"The guy worked his butt off all summer and actually ran this summer. He actually did like sprints and stuff. Came into camp in fantastic shape," Redick said.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"I think for someone who normally plays a ton of basketball, live basketball, he didn't do as much of that this summer by design. And I think we've seen him literally every day in camp, just incrementally just get more and more in rhythm," Redick added.

During his Dallas Mavericks stint, Doncic was frequently criticized for his conditioning and carrying extra weight. However, his arrival in Los Angeles has put him in a different conversation, with his offseason commitment becoming a major talking point.

His offseason work was evident in Sacramento, where Doncic looked comfortable and explosive despite playing limited minutes, finishing with 21 points. The Slovenian superstar also contributed two rebounds, three assists, and two steals.

The preseason numbers ultimately mean little compared with what happens during the regular season, but Doncic's performance in Sacramento offered an early indication that his offseason work could pay dividends.

The upcoming season also presents a new challenge for Doncic, as he is set to lead the LA team without LeBron James . Luka had already established himself as a franchise star even while James was alongside him in Los Angeles.

Now, it will be interesting to see whether Doncic can take another step forward and carry the Lakers into a new era as their unquestioned centerpiece.

articles.summary: Argentina is set to bid farewell to Lionel Messi in style, with Adidas releasing a special-edition kit to mark the occasion.

Argentina is set to bid farewell to Lionel Messi in style.

Messi will play his final match for Argentina on Tuesday, Oct. 6, as he suits up for his nation's friendly against Benin in Buenos Aires.

The 39-year-old announced his international retirement in August, but Argentina has called him up one final time to get a send-off in front of his home fans.

To commemorate the occasion, Adidas has released a special-edition jersey that Argentina will wear during the match at Estadio Monumental.

Argentina's traditional sky blue and white pattern is still present, but the narrow stripes have been replaced by wide stripes that mirror the country's flag.

The kits feature gold accents and lettering, drawing inspiration from the Sun of May in the center of Argentina's flag.

Messi's signature logo replaces the Adidas logo typically seen in the upper left portion of the jersey.

Messi goes into his final match as Argentina's record scorer with 125 goals and record appearance-maker with 207 caps.

The match kicks off at 7 p.m. ET and will be available to stream on ViX ( Watch on Prime Video ).

articles.title: Lions Make Decision on Brian Branch, Cade Mays
articles.summary: Brian Branch and Cade Mays will be designated to return and begin practicing this week, giving the Detroit Lions two potential reinforcements.
articles.body:
Help could finally be on the way for the Detroit Lions .

According to Ari Meirov , the Lions will designate safety Brian Branch and center Cade Mays to return from IR/PUP, opening the door for both players to begin practicing this week. Branch has been sidelined by an Achilles injury, while Mays has been recovering from the broken wrist that has kept him out since training camp.

For a Detroit team coming off a frustrating 32-26 loss to the Carolina Panthers , the timing couldn't be much better.

Brian Branch and Cade Mays Returning to Practice

The Branch news follows the encouraging update Dan Campbell provided Monday, when the Lions coach said, "I think it looks really good like Branch is going to practice this week." Getting Branch back would eventually provide a major boost for a Detroit defense that has allowed at least 30 points in three of its first four games.

Mays' return to practice is also significant. Campbell previously indicated that the Lions were targeting a return around the bye for their offseason addition, and getting Mays back on the field this week represents an important step toward strengthening Detroit's offensive line.

There is one important distinction, however. Being designated to return and beginning practice does not mean Branch or Mays will automatically play Sunday against the Arizona Cardinals.

The Lions have their bye in Week 6, so there is little reason to rush either player if the medical staff believes another couple of weeks would be beneficial. Detroit could allow Branch and Mays to practice this week, hold one or both out against Arizona, and then target a Week 7 return with additional recovery and practice time behind them.

The Lions badly need reinforcements. Two potentially important ones are officially getting closer.

articles.title: Bengals urged to ignore Joe Burrow after 'Let's throw it more' comment
articles.summary: This comment from Joe Burrow is one the Bengals should not listen to.
articles.body:
The Cincinnati Bengals lost in Week 4 to the Jacksonville Jaguars , dropping to 2-2 on the season, and tied with the Pittsburgh Steelers for last in the AFC North.

To get back above .500, the Bengals need to handle their business against the Miami Dolphins , which shouldn't be too difficult. But with uncertainty about Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins, Joe Burrow and the offense might be in some trouble.

That's all the more reason why the Bengals should listen to ESPN's Ben Solak's urging and ignore Burrow's comment about wanting to "throw it more" after a ridiculous 80-20 pass-run split in Week 4.

Bengals urged to ignore Joe Burrow's 'Let's throw it more' comment

"I think ... the Bengals need to ignore Joe Burrow about their pass-heavy approach," Solak writes.

After the Bengals' Week 4 matchup against the Jaguars, in which Cincinnati's offense threw the ball 81.7% of the time in the loss, Burrow was asked about that pass-heavy approach. His response? Burrow said, "Let's throw it more."

Burrow is a great quarterback and someone capable of throwing the ball 50 times a game if needed. But considering how bad of an idea that is long-term, the Bengals need to run the ball better this week.

With Chase Brown getting a weaker Dolphins defense, the Bengals should have no trouble running the ball effectively this upcoming week.

Add in the uncertainty of Chase and Higgins playing, which is further complicated by the looming Week 6 bye possibly incentivizing the Bengals to sit both WRs if they aren't 100%, and the Bengals might be forced to ignore Burrow's wishes.

While Burrow might be willing to throw the ball so much in every game, this isn't the recipe for a healthy offense. The Bengals have to get Brown and the run game going.

Solak is urging the Bengals to ignore Burrow's comment about wanting to throw the ball more, and there's no better week to do that than this one with a supposedly easy matchup against the lowly 0-4 Dolphins on tap.

articles.title: The Celtic connection to Spain’s last competitive defeat in 90 minutes
articles.summary: More than three years have passed since Spain were last beaten inside 90 minutes in a competitive match — and a look back at the Scotland team responsible sh...
articles.body:
More than three years have passed since Spain were last beaten inside 90 minutes in a competitive match — and a look back at the Scotland team responsible shows a considerable Celtic influence.

Steve Clarke's side stunned Spain 2-0 at Hampden in March 2023, with Scott McTominay scoring twice to secure one of Scotland's most memorable results of recent years.

The achievement has resurfaced after Football on TNT Sports highlighted Spain's remarkable unbeaten record since that night. For Celtic supporters, the Scotland line-up makes for interesting reading.

Callum McGregor played the full 90 minutes in midfield, with the Celtic captain lining up against a Spain side containing the likes of Rodri.

He was joined in the starting XI by then-two former Hoops teammates in Kieran Tierney and Ryan Christie.

Tierney was an Arsenal player at the time while Christie had already moved to Bournemouth, but both had previously been major figures at Parkhead.

Tierney and Christie were substituted during the second half, while McGregor remained on the pitch until the final whistle as Scotland completed their famous victory.

There were further Celtic connections on the bench, with Stuart Armstrong among Clarke's substitutes after starting the previous game against Cyprus.

Anthony Ralston had also initially been selected for the international window, although injury forced the Celtic defender to withdraw before the Spain clash.

McGregor was therefore the only Celtic player at the time to feature on the night, but the Hoops influence throughout Clarke's squad was clear.

Three years on, Tierney is back at Celtic alongside Ralston, with both going on to represent Scotland at the 2026 World Cup.

McGregor has since retired from international football after winning 63 caps, leaving that famous Hampden victory as one of the standout results of his Scotland career.

articles.title: Alabama basketball guard Aden Holloway reinstated, will play 2026-27 season
articles.summary: Alabama basketball guard Aden Holloway has been reinstated to the Crimson Tide's roster. What to know.
articles.body:
Look at our Alabama basketball vs Michigan photo gallery from Sweet 16

Alabama basketball guard Aden Holloway has been reinstated to the Crimson Tide's roster.

The senior entered a second-chance program following his arrest for marijuana possession in March, had his charges dismissed and has met the requirements necessary to rejoin Alabama on the floor.

Despite not officially being a member of the team as he navigated the legal process, Holloway was permitted to participate in summer workouts and has been involved with the 2026-27 squad.

Per a report from Al.com on Tuesday, Oct. 6, Holloway is rostered and "will be suspended for three exhibition games against Furman, Ole Miss and Auburn and two regular season games against Sam Houston and Arkansas State."

Holloway entered the second-chance program in an effort to clear his charges in June, which required court-mandated $150 monthly payments, 50 community service hours, as well as random drug and alcohol screenings.

In his second season at Alabama, Holloway shot better than 48% to average 16.8 points and 3.8 assists per game. He was arrested on March 16 for possessing 2.1 pounds of marijuana and failure to affix a tax stamp and was released on the same day.

The Crimson Tide officially starts the 2026-27 season Nov. 3 against Sam Houston in Coleman Coliseum.

articles.title: John Cena Classic Update, WWE Rumors on Damian Priest & Truth, WrestleMania & Royal Rumble Dates
articles.summary: Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe.
articles.body:
Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe.

Cena Reveals Timeline for John Cena Classic

Now or Never for LA Knight, More Raw Fallout 🗣️

After weeks and months of speculation, John Cena offered some confirmation this week regarding when the John Cena Classic will take place.

During an appearance on the Today show (h/t Subhojeet Mukherjee of Ringside News), Cena said the John Cena Classic tournament will be held in December.

Cena did not provide a specific date or any other previously unknown information, but the mention of December is the first official announcement regarding a timeline for the tourney since Cena first announced its existence at Backlash back in May.

Regarding what fans can expect out of the John Cena Classic, Cena told Today, "We're gonna do an event, based off all the memory, all the nostalgia, the I.P. and the core values of the character which is me: Hustle, loyalty, respect, perseverance, virtue, overcoming the odds and giving the vote to the people."

After first revealing the info at Backlash, Cena also doubled down on the declaration that the fans will decide the first John Cena Classic champion regardless of the results of the matches in the tournament.

Cena also added, "I don't even know if it's gonna work. I'm still taking bold chances in the WWE space and I'm proud to be helping the John Cena Classic."

Based on Cena's initial announcement of the John Cena Classic, he is hoping to help elevate young Superstars and take them to the next level in WWE.

That comes as little surprise given that Cena himself came up with the idea to feature NXT Superstars on the undercard of his retirement match against Gunther on Saturday Night's Main Event last December.

With the John Cena Classic slated for December 2026, it could be a great way to continue that mission, while also celebrating the one-year anniversary of Cena's retirement.

Reported Reason for Priest's Heel Turn on Truth

WWE reportedly made the decision to have Damian Priest turn heel on R-Truth in an effort to feature Priest in a more significant way.

According to WrestleVotes on Fightful Select (h/t Mukherjee ), WWE felt it had gone as far as it could go with the tag team of Priest and Truth, and that Priest being in a tag team was "reducing him rather than improving him."

WrestleVotes also reported that the Priest and Truth tag team was first conceived when Rhea Ripley went on the shelf with a knee injury.

WWE reportedly liked the idea of presenting Priest and Ripley as "The Terror Twins" on SmackDown, but when Ripley got hurt, something else was needed for Priest in the meantime.

Now, Priest is back on his own as a heel, and it could prove to be the best possible fit for him.

Most of Priest's greatest successes in WWE have come while he was a heel, particularly when he was part of The Judgment Day.

During that time, Priest won the Money in the Bank ladder match and successfully cashed it in to become world heavyweight champion.

While Priest and Truth did have a run as WWE tag team champions, there was little reason to keep them together any longer once they dropped the titles in August.

Reported Dates for Royal Rumble 2027, WrestleMania 43

WWE has yet to officially announce the dates for Royal Rumble 2027 or WrestleMania 43, but dates for both events may already be decided internally.

According to Fightful Select (h/t WrestlePurists ), sources believe Royal Rumble will be held the weekend of Feb. 6, 2027.

Meanwhile, Brandon Thurston and John Pollock of Post Wrestling (h/t Fightful's Sean Ross Sapp ) reported that WWE has internally listed the WrestleMania 43 dates as April 10 and 11, 2027.

The Royal Rumble date comes as little surprise given that WWE has been holding the event during the weekend between the NFL conference championship games and the Super Bowl for years.

This season, the Super Bowl is later than usual on Feb. 14, which necessitated the Rumble getting pushed into February rather than its usual late January date.

Royal Rumble could potentially take place either the day before or on the same day as AEW's Dynasty pay-per-view, which is scheduled for Feb. 7 in Liverpool, England.

As for WrestleMania, it is typically held in early April, although the past two years saw it take place a bit later in the month with WrestleMania 41 on April 19 and 20, and WrestleMania 42 on April 18 and 19.

WrestleMania 43 occurring on April 10 and 11 would be more in line with when the Showcase of the Immortals has traditionally happened.

Of course, WrestleMania 43 will feel much different than previous iterations since it is scheduled for Saudi Arabia, making it the first WrestleMania to ever be hosted outside the United States or Canada.
